“I have met very, very many leaders of the Arab and Islamic world, much more than you think, ” said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at a press conference last week.
Israeli Ambassador to the United States Ron Dermer told journalists that a breakthrough in relations with the UAE shows that Palestinian leaders can not stand between Tel Aviv and the Arab states.
“Rather than recognizing this reality and focusing on achieving a realistic compromise with Israel that will build a better future for both Israelis and Palestinians, unfortunately, these leaders remain mired in their rejection, they are stuck in the past, ” said Dermer.“ We hope that as the world expands into other Arab and Muslim countries, the situation will begin to change and the Palestinian society will emerge. more constructive forces ".
Indeed, solidarity with the Palestinians in their 70-year struggle for the territory with Israel has long dominated the political discourse of the Arab world.
However, the UAE ’ s decision to take a step towards Israel has caused much less controversy than the similar agreements concluded by Egypt in 1979 and Jordan in 1994.
Meanwhile, non-Arab regional players — Iran and Turkey — strongly supported Palestine.
Unlike the League of Arab States, these countries strongly criticized the actions of the UAE, calling Abu Dhabi ’ s decision to enter into an agreement with Israel hypocritical.
Palestine now hopes that other countries will not follow the example of the UAE.
“The failure of the League of Arab States to condemn the agreement on the normalization of relations between the UAE and Israel does not and does not imply the consent of the Member States to normalize relations with Israel, ” said Saeb Erekat, head of the Palestine Liberation Organization Negotiating Office, Newsweek.
Palestine, in its position, refers to international agreements — the Arab Peace Initiative of 2002, which calls for peace with Israel and an end to the Arab-Israeli conflict only if Israel withdraws from the territories it occupied in 1967 (including the Golan Heights and the Shab'a Farms) and recognizes the State of Palestine in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip with East Jerusalem as its capital.
“We hope that other Arab countries will not fall into normalization of relations with Israel.
Normalization has disastrous consequences for the future of the Palestinian cause, because it encourages Israel to strengthen and prolong the occupation of Palestine, not to put an end to it, ” Erekat said.
Palestine refers not only to the solidarity of the Arab world and international agreements, but also to the spread of the influence of the United States and Israel.
Thus, Erekat stressed that further progress in Tel Aviv ’ s relations with the Arab countries “will serve the extremist and ideological administrations of the United States and Israel, which seek to consolidate the apartheid system in Palestine, freeing the occupying Power, Israel, from the burden of retribution ”.
Faced with a serious divergence of views with the traditional allies, the Palestinians attempted to unite the internal fragmented forces in the hope of a united front.
On 3 September, a meeting of rival factions was held under the leadership of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas.
The conference also included representatives of the Palestine National Liberation Movement (Fatah) and the Palestinian Islamic Resistance Movement (Hamas).
“Our meeting is taking place at a very dangerous stage when our national affairs are confronted with various conspiracies and dangers, ” Abbas said.“ In order to stand together in the trenches of confrontation and peaceful popular resistance to occupation, I invite you to come and agree on the formation of national leadership. ”
The joint communiqué issued after the meeting called for the establishment of a “committee of eminent national personalities ”, which all parties trust to present a“ new strategic vision ” for the conflict with Israel.
Intra-Palestinian unity can pose new challenges to Israel, the United States, and even the League of Arab States.
“The Palestinian negotiating strategy and further steps will continue to be determined by the international legitimacy and vision of the two States within the 1967 borders, ” said Saeb Erekat.“ The achievement of Palestinian unity through the historic meeting of the Palestinian factions last week is a step towards unifying the Palestinian position against the plans for annexation of Israel, the Trump plan and all attempts to normalize the Israeli occupation of Palestine. ”
In one way or another, Arab countries are moving further away from anti-Israeli positions, especially against the background of the growing influence of neighbouring Shia Iran, which has become a much more serious problem for Sunni countries.
As noted by the expert of the Carnegie Center in Moscow, Alexei Malashenko, the solidarity of the Arab world called for by Palestine, has never been real.
“There have always been national interests, including in relation to the Middle East conflict, including in relation to Israel.
This trend has not begun today.
Therefore, I think that today Israel is not a factor that could rally around Arabs at the state level, ” the expert notes. “To say that the entire Arab world in general is enthusiastic, I would not, but the heads of state, of course, are the majority for [normalizing relations with Israel], because the conflict is boring everyone, there are quite other problems, the same Islamic extremists.
Therefore, if we look at the future, relations between the Arabs and Israel will generally improve. ”

Title: Will Putin go to the "deal of the century" with Israel and the United States

Content: MOSCOW, 30 Jan — RIA Novosti, Galia Ibragimova, Sofia Melnichuk.
Bingyamin Netanyahu arrives in Moscow when he returns from the United States.
He intends to reveal at a meeting with Vladimir Putin the details of the "deal of the century" on the Arab-Israeli settlement.
The Russian Foreign Ministry has already made it clear that the deal will not take place without the approval of the Palestinian side.
However, Netanyahu has another goal, which is also quite delicate.
"The greatest friend of Israel", Putin and Netanyahu met last week in Jerusalem at Holocaust remembrance events.
But the plan for a Palestinian-Israeli settlement, developed and published recently in the United States, the Israeli prime minister considered a significant reason to meet with the Russian president again.
Netanyahu hopes that Moscow ’ s assessment of Washington and Tel Aviv ’ s peacekeeping initiatives can affect their perception in the world.
But most importantly, the opinion of Russia, which has always been authoritative in the Arab world, can be listened to by Palestinians.
However, the Kremlin has so far been very reluctant to respond to the deal presented by the Donald Trump administration.
Special Representative of the Russian President for the Middle East and Africa, Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Bogdanov said that it was too early to draw any conclusions.
"We believe that we must enter into direct negotiations (with the Palestinians) and reach mutually acceptable compromises.
We do not know how much Washington's ideas are mutually acceptable to all parties to the conflict, "Bogdanov explained the position of the Russian side.
We should also listen to the opinion of the "quartet" on the Middle East settlement - the EU, the USA, Russia, the United Nations, emphasized in Moscow.
Brussels himself was not unwilling to participate in the preparation of the plan.
However, Trump refused to help intermediaries.
The document was written by his advisor and son-in-law, Jared Kouchner.
The latter, in turn, took account mainly of Israel's position.
"There is nothing more difficult in the world than reconciling Israelis and Palestinians.
But I didn't become president to deal with minor issues.
"Deal of the century" is beneficial to both sides, and this is a huge step towards peace, "the President of the United States said at the presentation of the long-awaited settlement plan.
"You have shown yourself as Israel's greatest friend ever to be in the White House," reacted to Netanyahu's deal, wholeheartedly supporting her.
© REUTERS / Joshua Roberts US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a joint press conference in Washington © REUTERS / Joshua Roberts US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a joint press conference in Washington The essence of the deal The 181-page text of the "deal of the century" consists of political and economic sections.
The political part of the document is based on the principle of "two States for two peoples": along with Israel, Palestine will appear on the map of the world.
The document stipulates that Jerusalem should become the indivisible capital of Israel.
At the same time, the sovereignty of the Jewish State may extend to a significant part of the Jordan Valley.
Trump believes that the “bargain of the century ” is also beneficial to the Arabs, as it suggests that East Jerusalem be the capital of the Palestinians.
According to the map of the division of territories annexed to the "transaction", they are neighborhoods outside the separation fence built by Israel.
The old city will not enter the borders of the Palestinian capital.
“If the deal is implemented, the Palestinian territories will double the ones they control today, ” Trump explained.
The divided lands of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, according to Americans, can be connected by tunnels.
And the airspace over these territories will be controlled by the Palestinians.
But before that, they must recognize Palestine as a demilitarized State.
"Transaction" also implies a number of requirements for Israel.
The main thing is to recognize the independence of Palestine.
The construction of new settlements in the West Bank will have to be frozen for four years.
The economic part of the deal revolves around projects to be implemented in the West Bank, the Gaza Strip, Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon.
The investment will be $50 billion.
This money, according to Washington's calculations, will give the Palestinians Arab monarchies of the Persian Gulf.
The authors of the "deal" and the assistance of private capital are expected.
This is what a future State of Palestine can look like, with a capital in parts of East Jerusalem.
pic.twitter.com / 39vw3pPrAL — Donald J. Trump (@ realDonaldTrump) January 28, 2020 "Jerusalem is not for sale" Neither before nor after the publication of the "deal" information has any country expressed its willingness to invest in potential projects in Palestine.
Moreover, most countries in the Middle East have criticized the document.
"Jerusalem is not sold, Palestinian rights are not sold and cannot be traded.
Your deal is a conspiracy and it will not pass, "the head of the Palestinian Authority, Mahmoud Abbas, outraged.
"Trump and his" deal of the century "place in the dump of history.
The document is not even worth the ink that is written, "said Sami Abu Zuhri, a representative of the Hamas movement that controls the Gaza Strip.
In disagreement, the Palestinians protested.
In the Gaza Strip, rallies began a few days before the presentation of the document.
Turkey and Iran strongly criticized the initiative.
Egypt and Jordan called for "a closer examination of the document".
Opinions have also been divided in Europe.
Germany, France, Sweden supported American peacekeeping efforts, but condemned the one-sided — pro-client — view of the problem.
The "deal" was supported by the United Kingdom.
"The developed plan is an important step in the right direction," said Boris Johnson.
© REUTERS / Ibraheem Abu Mustafa Protest action against the Palestinian-Israeli settlement plan in the southern Gaza Strip © REUTERS / Ibraheem Abu Mustafa Protest action against the Palestinian-Israeli settlement plan in the southern Gaza Strip Remove an Israeli woman from prison There is also another reason why Netanyahu arrives in Moscow.
On the eve of Israeli politics, it was not ruled out that the Prime Minister planned to be present in person when the compatriot Naama Issahar was released.
In autumn, a 26-year-old Israeli woman was detained in the transit zone of Sheremetyevo airport.
Nine grams of hashish were found in her luggage and sentenced to seven years in prison.
The case has caused a lot of public attention.
Issachar ’ s mother appealed to the President of Russia for a pardon.
"Everything will be fine," Putin promised her.
A couple of days ago her mother arrived in Russia, and a day later it became known about the visit to Moscow of the Israeli Prime Minister.
The day before, Putin pardoned Naama Issachar, and this morning she was released.
Unequal world and electoral ratings The experts interviewed by RIA Novosti agreed that the central topic of Putin and Netanyahu ’ s talks will still be the “deal of the century ”.
But they warned that Moscow's skeptical attitude towards the American-Israeli initiative is unlikely to change.
"It's a completely intractable document.
It violates the rights of Palestinians to part of Jerusalem, which are laid down by the UN Security Council resolution.
The American plan has not been approved by international organizations, nor has it been approved by the Palestinians.
The General Sec of the League of Arab States recognized that the rights of Palestinians in the transaction are infringed, "said Vitaly Naumkin, Scientific Director of the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences, in an interview with RIA Novosti.
In order to hear the views of the Palestinians, the expert believes that it would be useful to combine the efforts of Fatah (a paramilitary organization and a political party) and Hamas.
"These organizations, which run the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, it is now appropriate to agree among themselves and to agree on a common point of view on the American plan.
Then they can be heard.
But the problem is that the division within the Palestinians is hampering the advancement of their own interests in this difficult situation, "Naumkin stressed.
Middle East specialist political scientist Nurlan Gasimov notes that the deal involves the transfer to Israeli control of a significant part of the West Bank.
"The territory is now divided into three zones: A, B and C. Area A comprises about 17 per cent of the land controlled by Palestinians.
Zone B is under the joint control of Palestinians and Israelis.
And the largest zone C includes almost 60 per cent of the territory and is fully controlled by Israel.
In this case, it is in zone C that fertile lands are located.
But the most important thing is that all the fresh water supplies are concentrated there.
As early as 1993, Israel, in signing an agreement in Oslo to resolve the conflict with the Palestinians, drew up a map in such a way as to settle the territories suitable for that purpose.
Trump ’ s “Deal of the Century ” aims at the final transition of these lands to Israel.
It turns out that Palestinians will be denied access to fresh water, "Gasimov explains.
The territories in which Trump proposes to create the state of Palestine, according to a political scientist, are divided enclaves.
"Basically these are the lands in zones A and B. But even if they are connected by bridges and tunnels, Israel can easily block them at any time.
In addition, it is difficult to manage dispersed territories from the point of view of public administration.
It is also difficult to develop any economic projects there.
This damage is understood by both Palestinians and Israelis and Americans, "explains Gasimov.
The settlement plan, according to the expert, is also designed for domestic audiences in Israel and the United States.
"The process of impeachment of the President continues in the States.
There will be a third election in Israel.
From here, both Trump and Netanyahu benefit from mobilizing the right electorate through the "deal of the century", he said.
Ksenia Svetlova, an ex-Knesset member and expert at the Herzliya Interdisciplinary Institute in Israel, agrees that the initiative under discussion is part of Netanyahu's election campaign.
"Netanyahu flew to the United States before the Knesset meeting.
Parliamentarians are going to consider granting immunity to the Prime Minister in connection with corruption charges.
Depriving him now is extremely unprofitable.
For many Israelis, it seems that there are no urgent circumstances that would justify the Prime Minister ’ s visits to the United States or Russia.
Especially since the "deal of the century" was formed about a year and a half ago and was postponed all the time, "says Svetlova.

The medical tourism industry in Seoul is engaged in microsurgery and cosmetic surgery.

The reason is clear.
The cost of treatment in underdeveloped countries is three times lower than in developed countries.
In our area, medical tourism in India is growing rapidly.
Statistics show that in 2004, 1.2 million patients traveled to India for health care, and 1.1 million medical tourists traveled to Thailand.
While increasing GDP, economic development, creating job opportunities are among the benefits of this industry, Iran can also be cited as a result of a combination of medical and recreational tourism and the existence of historical and ancient monuments, pilgrimage centers and natural beauty and natural treatments (traditional medicine).
But the lack of advertising and branding overseas medical tourism as well as the presence of unauthorized health tourism mediators and institutions has put the industry in serious harm.
The issue that has recently become a significant point for top managers and even officials of the Ministry of Health to think about the development of the medical tourism industry.
As the activists of this field say, one of the important concerns and challenges in this field is the correct and correct guidance of foreign patients to medical centers of Iran, so that medical tourists do not get involved with the dealer from the moment they enter the country, non-medical interventions will not be conducted by doctors for cosmetic surgery applicants and eventually medical tourists will be able to advertise Iranian medical services by receiving standard medical services in reputable medical centers.
On the general role and policies of the Ministry of Health in the development of medical tourism, challenges and opportunities to attract and follow up patients from the country of origin to Iran, we talked with Dr. Saeed Hashemzadeh, head of the Health Tourism Department of the Ministry of Health, which you can read below.
How medical tourists (Medical Tourism) are attracted to medical centers of Iran?
I mean, because of the presence of intermediaries, foreign patients are not properly directed to medical centers and are not reached by specialists, and sometimes we hear that they fall into the hands of agents and institutions that are not allowed, and they are leading the applicants of these types of surgeries to people who are not qualified.
Is there a specific model for guiding the patient to medical centers that the medical tourist does not receive non-standard medical services and is not directed to invalid medical centers?
We at the Ministry of Health believe that brokers are not causes, but disabled.
So if we want to deal with a broker ’ s phenomenon in the field of health tourism, we ’ ll simply ask the police to stop the dealer ’ s work, but we don ’ t believe this will cause the dealer ’ s work to go away.
So we tried to identify the drawbacks that exist in the supply chain in health tourism, and then, based on that, the dealers are out of the industry.
Of course, I have to say, the health centers of the country have capabilities and capabilities, but they could not properly introduce and supply these capabilities abroad, where our customers are present.
Now, who gives the foreign patient information about what medical and medical care is done under what conditions and at what cost?
The answer to this question is clear: an element found in the name of the broker.
Because of this gap or lack of information between health centers and patients abroad, an element called the broker plays this role.
In order to systematically undermine the field of dealer activity, it is enough to see who is acting in the successful models of the world and who is going to deliver this information to the patient to reduce the field of dealer activity.
When we look at successful models in West Asia, including India, Turkey and Jordan, we see an actor here called "Facilitator Company."
The main task of facilitating companies is to provide medical information from medical centers and physicians and to inform about transparent prices to foreign patients. With this knowledge, we designed the regulations to form companies that work professionally in this field, namely, these companies play a role in deciding for patients who enter the country, then facilitate the arrival of the patient to the country and after receiving medical services from the patient external, follow up after treatment.
Of course, follow-up after treatment is an important part of the work that has been forgotten in our country, which means we didn ’ t have regular and structured follow-up, so we started doing the same thing.
Facilitator companies attract medical tourism have a specific channel to attract foreign patients, how do these companies shorten dealers and intermediaries in this field?
These companies are licensed by the Ministry of Health to attract different types of foreign patients to Iranian health centers.
In cyberspace, such as the website and social networks, they start to work and inform the people of foreign countries about the capabilities of the health centers on the sides of their contract in cyberspace.
The second solution is to attend national and international health tourism exhibitions and events.
The third solution is to join similar companies in the target markets.
That is, Iranian companies connect to their similar companies in Iraq and Afghanistan, through which they refer the patient to our country.
A very important solution is the joining of facilitators to insurance companies on the other side of the border, which, of course, has not been noticed in our country.
This means that we have little actor here, and that is the connection of foreign insurance companies to Iran facilitators to attract patients in international markets in an organized manner.
This is the model that's being done in all countries.
In our country, which of these channels you mentioned provides a way to attract foreign patients?
Apart from the type of broker, the kind that is so stressed is attracting the patient through cyberspace.
Still seems to have a larger share of brokers in attracting foreign patients?
Do you have any statistics on how many medical tourism tourists enter Iran ’ s treatment centers through brokers?
It is not more than 5 months since facilitator ’ s regulations have been communicated. It should take some time to make the right comparison.
Most of the patients who enter the treatment centers are by these same brokers, but the balance changes in the interest of the companies.
Between 80 and 90 percent of patients were brought by brokers, and the share of direct patient referral is less than 10 percent.
The weight is now shifting towards the companies.
The medical centers have reported the same thing to us, the centers that used to say that 90 percent of foreign patients come to Iran through brokers now say 70 percent of them come to the country through brokers.
The trend of change, though low, has started, which means 10 percent of the market is accounted for by companies, while we only licensed 15 percent of these companies.
If the insurance is added to this supply chain, this will accelerate.
You mentioned connecting Iranian facilitators to foreign insurance companies to attract medical tourism.
Since the arrival of medical tourists in Iran, how is the process of receiving their services?
Please tell us if a medical visa is issued easily for patients?
Are they offered unaccompanied services and VIP services?
On the basis of what process the patient enters the medical center of the foreign country, let me first tell you the model of the world.
Usually, this is how the patient travels to another country to receive a special service that is not covered by insurance.
For example, in Europe, if a person with a doctor 's diagnosis needs knee replacement and this service is not covered by insurance, the insurance department recommends to the patient to use the company' s consulting facilitator and to go to India or Turkey for knee replacement, in which case, the knee replacement service is covered by the insurance of the country of origin, that is, the person does not have any insurance coverage for joint replacement in Europe, but in India and Turkey can receive this service. The insurance mode not only pays the patient ’ s expenses, but also provides airline tickets and accommodation costs.
For example, in the United States, knee replacement costs $220,000, but if this patient goes to India with the best hotel and plane and the best service costs $15,000 for his insurance company.
Almost the same cycle should be implemented in our country.
We will succeed in medical tourism when we can implement the same general cycle. For now, the process of working is that the disease, which is recommended in Iraq, does medical work, enters Iran.
If it is placed in a healthy cycle, with advertising companies in cyberspace, the patient chooses to enter into which city and hospital, then the patient contracts with the facilitator and the company coordinates the work of obtaining a visa, ticket, accommodation and displacement of the patient and the patient enters Iran and after receiving service to his country, the treatment is followed by the facilitator company.
What we need to do is that the patient in his home and in his life decides which Iranian medical center to go to.
It is interesting to know that since the new generation facilitator companies that the Ministry of Health permits have been created, we have faced an increase in patient visits from Europe.
European patients who choose Iranian cosmetic surgeries and take all their information from cyberspace and enter Iran through facilitators are closer to the international health tourism model about attracting European patients.
This pattern should also be extended about neighboring patients to allow patients to enter a safe corridor.
As for insurance, so far, they have not played an important role in the field of health tourism except in the case of specific European patients.
What are the reasons for choosing medical centers in Iran? What types of surgeries are they looking for, and from what countries are applicants often entering medical centers in Iran?
According to statistics about patients admitted to medical centers, most of our health tourists come to Iran from Afghanistan, Iraq, Azerbaijan, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, India and Turkmenistan.
Of course, Iranians residing abroad come to Iran for their health care, which is also considered as health tourists.
The citizens of these countries refer to the cities of the country or universities of medical sciences, respectively, Iran University of Medical Sciences, Mashhad, Qom, Shahid Beheshti University, Shiraz, Ahvaz, Urmia, Tabriz, Tehran and Semnan.

Title: During the pandemic, residents of megacities began to appreciate more "islands of nature"

Content: Sociologists interviewed residents of Moscow and Perth to find out what role urban green zones played for them during the pandemic.
It turned out that most respondents in both cities considered contact with nature to be essential for mental well-being, and many of them went on walks in their free time despite restrictions.
The results of the research supported by the RNF grant are published in the journal Sustainability.
For more than a year, the daily lives of people around the world have been subject to the strict rules of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Access green areas and water facilities were a particularly important component of urban infrastructure under quarantine conditions.
So far, the impact of the pandemic on the role of green areas in the lives of citizens has been studied, mainly on the example of large European cities, which is not enough for a comprehensive assessment of the situation.
Therefore, sociologists drew their attention to the comparison of such radically different in terms of climate, culture and infrastructure of megacities as Moscow and Perth.
Researchers from the Peoples' Friendship University of Russia (Moscow) and their foreign colleagues conducted a survey among 330 residents of Moscow and Perth, Australia.
The questionnaire contained 25 questions about the role of urban green areas and water bodies in the daily life of people, the impact of quarantine on their pastime and well-being, as well as possible ways to develop the green areas of the city.
According to the data received, more than 50 per cent of the residents of Moscow and 72 per cent of the residents of Perth during the pandemic, despite restrictions, preferred to spend their free time on a walk.
At the same time, it should be emphasized that there was a significant difference in the degree of quarantine measures between the cities under study: in Perth, urban green areas (public parks, reserves, gardens, beaches) were opened during the entire period of the pandemic of 2020, while in Moscow for 1.5 months there was a complete ban on visiting public places.
This is due to the difference in the frequency of visits to green areas during quarantine: in Moscow, 56.9 per cent of respondents rarely visited green areas, while 59.4 per cent of Perth residents did not change their frequency of visits, and 26.7 per cent even increased.
However, immediately after the removal of restrictive measures in Moscow, the attendance of green areas relative to the pre-quarantine period increased significantly.
At the same time, residents of both cities stressed the importance of urban green areas in their daily lives.
Most respondents in both Moscow and Perth assessed contact with nature as important or very important for physical and mental well-being (more than 97 per cent of Perth respondents indicated significance for mental and 85 per cent for physical well-being, and more than 76 and 70 per cent of Moscow respondents, respectively).
Asked about the current state and possible improvements in urban green areas, most respondents from both Moscow (55 per cent) and Perth (77 per cent) indicated that street gardening activities would be the most desirable for them.
Also a popular variant of the answer was an increase in the number of public parks and green spaces near their own houses.
With regard to infrastructure, respondents in both cities indicated the need for more benches, as well as shady places and rain canopies.
Residents of Moscow additionally noted the need to create water bodies (fountains and ponds) and gazebos, as well as modern elements of the landscape, such as green walls.
This highlights the importance of improving urban green areas to improve both the urban environment itself and the well-being of its inhabitants.
Analyzing the attitude of residents of Moscow and Perth to green areas and water facilities within the city, we can conclude that, despite the differences in climate and socio-economic situation, the availability of "natural islands" is highly appreciated by all respondents.
This confirms the idea that greening plays a critical role in ensuring the sustainability of cities in times of crisis, including the COVID-19 pandemic.
“In our research, we wanted to emphasize that urban greening and environmental issues in general should be fully developed and included in policy documents aimed at the strategic development of urban agglomerations.
For modern urban dwellers, places are essential to enable them to maintain their health and well-being.
These places, based on the results of our research, are parks, urban forests, squares, landscaped courtyards - green spaces in the open air.
Rational planning of these sites will not allow them to be closed in crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic, but, on the contrary, make them accessible.
This will be crucial for improving the overall sustainability of cities, ” concludes Anastasia Konstantinova, RNF grant project manager, Candidate of Sociological Sciences, researcher at Smart Urban Nature laboratory at the Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Due to the severe constraints on the development of the Arab region, the Turkish drama has begun to take a look at the world in recent years. The Turkish drama was later expanded to broadcast in many European countries, such as Italy.
Jose Antonio Anton, vice president of the Atresmedia Group, a Spanish media group that introduced local dramas, believes that Turkey is a country that combines modern and traditional aspects, and that these elements are fully reflected in local dramas, thus helping the world to understand the country.
In addition, the Turkish television industry has a large budget, excellent scenes, excellent acting and outdoor studios, which have been able to produce a high level of television in the past 20 years.
In recent years, local dramas have also turned to other platforms such as the Internet and Netflix. At the same time, local dramas have changed beyond the target audience, and the variety of dramas has tended to be diverse.

Turkey has surpassed Mexico and Brazil as the world ’ s second largest television exporter after the United States, with exports across Europe, the Arab region, Central Asia and the Americas. To date, Turkey has contributed more than 150 television productions to about 500 million viewers in 146 countries.
It is estimated that the total value of Turkish drama exports reached US $500 million (about HK $3.9 billion) last year, and television exports are expected to reach US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion) by 2023.

Saudi Arabia is expected to expand other areas of culture in the future, encouraging arts, musical performances, and other forms of entertainment.

It is estimated that the country will have about 350 cinemas and 2,500 movie screens in 2030, with an industry value of about US $1 billion (about HK $7.8 billion).
The country also plans to double household entertainment spending, from 3% of GDP in 2018-2019 to 6% in 2030.
Saudi Arabia, on the other hand, has cooperated with the United Arab Emirates in the development of the video industry.
Among them, the two governments co-financed a US $40 million (HK $310 million) drama, Kingdoms of Fire, which aired in 2019, highlighting the Ottoman Empire as a tyrant who has destroyed the Arab world for centuries.
In addition to partnering in the production of the film, the long-term partnership between the media companies of the two countries also includes training of film producers and performing artists.

Many people see the growing growth of film and television in countries and regions, and no longer object to their children enrolling in relevant courses, and think that they can find the ideal job after graduation.
Mohamed Ghazala, president of the School of Film and Television Arts at Effat University in Saudi Arabia, said: "The growing demand for local talent and capacity will open the way for more departments and research institutes in Saudi Arabia." However, the Saudi film industry is also facing a number of problems, with 43% of the industry saying that it is largely lacking. Thirteen percent said they lacked manpower, and 11 percent said they lacked video-related training and education.
Currently, the industry ’ s main funding and arts support comes from three government-funded organizations: King Abdulaziz Center for World Cultures, the Film and Television Committee of the Bureau of Culture, and the Red Sea Film Festival.
Saudi director Hana Alomair stated, "We are hungry for more, we are still talking about government support, and investors have yet to take practical action."
She added that the increase in the number of cinemas should help encourage investment.
King Mohammed has been actively developing the Saudi television industry in recent years.
(Reuters) The war on soft power tells the story of the Arab world. In fact, Saudi Arabia is vigorously developing the film and television industry and shooting high quality television series. In addition to economic reform, Saudi Arabia hopes to create a national image through the film and television industry, promote its own views and values, and avoid the Turkish side's exclusive occupation of the Middle East.
This is obviously due to the fact that over the past 10 years, Turkey has been able to invest heavily in the film and television industry.
Yu s e r Hareb, a Saudi Arabian-based film producer, argues that Saudi development of the video industry is an attempt to create alternative options to counteract the influence of Turkish drama on Arabs.
He argued that the Ottoman period was not a glorious one for the Arabs, or even a "dark one", full of repression and criminal acts against the Arabs.
The work of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates is intended to break the cultural influence of Turkey in the region by telling "true Arab history" that Osman is neither a protector nor a reincarnation of Muslims.
Saudi Arabia also wants to export cultural influence through the video industry. (Getty) Saudi Arabia ’ s “war ” says that both sides want to influence the Middle East by promoting their national identity and culture. Both countries want to beautify history and influence audiences, especially in which country should be praised and reprimanded.
However, Saudi Arabia's development of the film and television industry is short, and it seems difficult to say whether it will be able to resist the influence of Turkey, both in the region and around the world, by virtue of its film and television productions.

Title: The Mars Rover Perseverance has successfully tested the instrument for extracting oxygen from the Martian atmosphere

Content: An experimental device called MOXIE (Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment) was first tested on April 20, and this test was recognized as successful: in an hour of operation, the installation the size of a conventional toaster was able to produce more than 5 grams of oxygen, writes Newsru.
The atmosphere of Mars is almost 96% carbon dioxide (CO2).
The MOXIE plant is able to process this carbon dioxide into oxygen and carbon monoxide (CO, carbon monoxide), which is a by-product of processing and is thrown back into the atmosphere.
The process of processing carbon dioxide occurs by electrolysis of solid oxides at a temperature of 800 degrees Celsius.
During operation, the device captures carbon dioxide, passes through a dust removal filter and compresses it, providing pressure at the ground level.
Then gas passes through heated cell of electrolysis, which consists of several layers of nickel alloy and ceramics.
The ceramic elements of the cell are able to conduct current at high temperature - they pass oxygen ions and trap carbon monoxide.
The outer surface of MOXIE is covered with a thin layer of gold.
This coating protects the MOXIE surface from heating, protecting the electronics of the rover located next to the device.
Future astronauts: breathe easier.
The MOXIE technology demonstration aboard @ NASAPerSevere successfully extracted oxygen from the thin Martian atmosphere — a critical component for life support on the Red Planet and rocket fuel for the trip home. https: / / t.co / sguhYgkP pic.twitter.com / SwL0etf9Uu — NASA JPL (@ NASAJPL) April 21, 2021 MOXIE ’ s maximum design capacity is up to 10 grams of oxygen per hour.
The test program of the instrument provides for at least nine more tests over a period of two years.

Title: Oxygen and hydrogen on Mars proposed to be obtained from brine

Content: Scientists have developed a method of obtaining oxygen and hydrogen from a liquid salt solution in the conditions of the Martian lakes using electrolysis.
A feature of the experiment was the use of lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst for oxygen production.
The generation of oxygen through this plant was 25 times more energy efficient than in the case of MOXIE launched to the Red Planet within the framework of the Mars 2020 mission, and the size and weight of the life-support device based on the described technology will be less than in analogues.
The article is published in the journal PNAS.
The conditions on Mars are far from favorable to humans: the atmosphere is discharged and 95 percent consists of carbon dioxide, and temperature differences exceed 100 degrees Celsius at an average temperature of minus 63 degrees.
Therefore, colonization of the Red Planet is impossible without the creation of a life-support system that would, under such harsh conditions, be able to provide people with oxygen for breathing and fuel (for example, hydrogen) for energy supply and, ideally, return flight.
To solve the first problem, NASA created MOXIE (Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment), an experimental plant for producing oxygen from atmospheric carbon dioxide by electrolysis.
To test the effectiveness of such a method in the field, the installation became part of the Mars Rover Perseverance, which was launched on July 30, 2020 as part of the Mars 2020 mission.
An alternative source of not only oxygen, but also hydrogen on Mars can be water, the first direct evidence of the existence of which on the Red planet was obtained as early as 1971.
Particularly attractive for applications, however, would be saline water reserves, where impurities would allow it to remain liquid even at low temperatures and pressures.
The first traces of such a brine (liquid salt solution) with magnesium perchlorate as the main component were found on Mars in 2015, and in 2018 under the polar ice of the planet found a reservoir with a diameter of about 20 kilometers, which could be formed due to volcanic activity.
Planetologists later confirmed that such lakes on Mars really exist and can be numerous.
Now Pralay Gayen from the University of Washington, St. Louis, together with his colleagues, has created a plant to obtain oxygen and hydrogen from a saline solution close in composition and temperature to that in the Martian lakes.
As a brine, the experiment used a solution of magnesium perchlorate in water with a concentration of 2.8 mol per liter, cooled to minus 36 degrees Celsius and blown out with carbon dioxide (the latter played the role of the Martian atmosphere).
As an oxygen generation electrocatalyst, scientists used lead-ruthenium oxide Pb2Ru2O7-δ, the efficiency of which they previously showed for alkaline solutions.
The electrocatalyst for hydrogen production was platinum on activated carbon, the standard catalyst in this case, and the commercially released anion-exchange membrane was used as a separator.
Installation scheme.
In the red region, oxygen is produced, in the blue - hydrogen.
Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS In the course of the study, scientists have shown that lead-ruthenium oxide as an electrocatalyst is really much more effective than usually used in such installations of ruthenium oxide.
After the behavior of the plant was studied in a wide range of temperatures from − 36 to 21 degrees Celsius and saw no radical fluctuations in efficiency and rate of production.
The current output of the experimental plant was 70 per cent, and the energy efficiency was between 36 and 70 per cent (depending on the voltage supplied to the plates).
In addition, the plant was resistant to the degradation of the catalyst: scientists failed to find traces of ruthenium in the solution after 300 minutes of operation of the device.
The rate of production of oxygen (blue dots) and hydrogen (red dots) depending on the density of the cathode current.
Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Also, researchers compared the achieved rate of oxygen production with the MOXIE values of 10-22 grams per hour: it turned out that with the same energy supply, the created unit produces 25 times more oxygen than the experiment on the Mars Rover "Perseverance".
In order to have the same rate of oxygen production as MOXIE, the device would have to have electrodes with an area of 28-62 square centimeters, and to ensure the viability of a sleeping and actively moving person, this parameter would have to be 375 and 1,335 square centimeters, respectively.
At the same time, the mass and volume of the installation will be less than if you use the technology embedded in MOXIE.
Moreover, the developed method of obtaining oxygen does not require its subsequent purification, while in the course of electrolysis, MOXIE produces carbon monoxide, which needs to be filtered.
Dependence on the power consumption of the rate of oxygen generation of the plant (blue line), as well as its cape and volume to provide various modes of human activity (black lines).
The blue point is the power and rate of oxygen generation at MOXIE.
Image source: Pralay Gayen et al. / PNAS Earlier we talked about another method of producing oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere (as MOXIE): scientists suggested to do this using low-temperature plasma.
And what is the role of the Mars Rover Perseverance in addition to testing the method of producing oxygen, you can read in our material "Mars, there and back."
Nikita Kozyrev

Title: It is time to change the packaging of household chemicals

Content: Checking the KROT household fluid has begun.
As a result, an opinion will be submitted.
Rossiyskaya Gazeta reported this in Rospotrebnadzor.
Resonance of poisoning by means of cleaning pipes of famous producer and musician Bari Alibasov revealed a serious problem: packaging of hazardous household chemicals can pose a threat to human life and health.
And the rules of its registration must be changed.
As explained in Rospotrebnadzor, today the requirements for marking household chemicals are contained in the Unified Sanitary-Epidemiological and Hygienic Requirements for Products (Goods) subject to Sanitary-Epidemiological Supervision (Control).
For example, consumer labeling of synthetic detergents and household chemicals should be applied in clear, legible, easily visible and indelible letters, resistant to chemicals, climatic factors, remain for the entire life of the product.
Bottles with household chemicals, in particular, should contain information on the composition of products and "other data that make it possible to clearly distinguish a particular product from other products on the market".
There should also be a description of the danger posed by such products, measures to prevent danger.
For example, such inscriptions: "Keep away from children!", "Keep out of reach of children", "The product has an irritating effect on the skin", "The use of hand protection means is mandatory".
"I am sure that all household chemicals that are sold in stores are of high quality and meet the marking requirements.
After all, no one will knowingly harm the health of consumers, creating anti-advertising for themselves.
But life, as always, makes its adjustments, - said the Chairman of the Consumer Union of Russia Peter Shelisch in a conversation with "RG". - The case with Alibasov has proved: the packaging of some household chemicals needs to be changed.
I saw a picture taken by someone in Alibasov's environment with a bottle of liquid to clean pipes and yogurt.
I think it's quite easy to confuse them. "
Shelisch reminds me that there are very catchy "terrible pictures" and large inscriptions on cigarette packs.
And on the packages of household chemicals, warning signs still need to be found and read.
"Yes, they comply with all the rules, but therefore these rules and regulations are not enough to protect the consumer," the expert notes. "Unfortunately, there are no statistics on how many people are poisoned with household chemicals.
But according to scattered reports, it can be understood that the case with Alibasov is not the only one.
Perhaps you need to write in very large letters on packages that their contents can not be drunk.
And even better to make difficult opening plugs.
Manufacturers of medicines make them for the protection of children. "
The producer's relatives intend to sue the manufacturer with the means to clean the pipes.
How real will it be to win a case in court?
"The case with Alibasov is regrettable, I wish him a speedy recovery," says Denis Frolov, head of commercial practice of the law firm. "But filing a lawsuit against the manufacturer - it will be a PR action rather than a real attempt to obtain compensation.
The products of household chemicals are always indicated instructions for use and warnings in case of their violation.
If the consumer, despite this, confuses these goods with edible products, the manufacturer is not guilty of this.
However, the court will accept the claim if it formally complies with the requirements of the law.
Another thing is that there is virtually no prospect of such a case, as there is no basis under existing law for satisfying the plaintiff's claims. "
But in any case, it will draw attention to the problem.
And the marking rules will still be tightened, as Peter Shelisch suggests.
And how they have Billions for deceptive packaging, the California Courts in the United States have, over the past few months, obligated Monsanto, a member of the Bayer structure, to pay huge compensation to consumers for the absence of warnings on the carcinogenicity packaging of one of its products.
This is a glyphosate, a worldwide weed removal agent known as the "Roundup" trademark.
For example, in May, a jury jury awarded astronomical compensation of $2 billion to a couple from California Auckland.
Before that, a San Francisco court ordered Monsanto pay 80 million dollars to farmer Edwin Hardman.
The lion ’ s share of this payment is a fine for the fact that Monsanto, according to the jury, deliberately did not make appropriate warnings on the packaging and, moreover, sponsored studies that proved the safety of this herbicide.
The victims claimed that due to the absence of warnings on the package, glyphosate was sprayed for years and without danger allowed the substance to fall on unprotected skin.
Later, they were diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and, as the jury considered, it was the herbicide that was to blame.
Monsanto insists that studies clearly do not confirm the carcinogenicity of glyphosate and fiercely contests these resonant verdicts.
After all, several thousand similar lawsuits are now waiting for their turn in the courts.

Content: German chemical and pharmaceutical company Bayer has reached a settlement with a number of plaintiffs in the United States over a legal dispute over a herbicide containing glyphosate.
The company announced the announcement, saying it would pay between US $10.1 billion and US $10.9 billion.
The move could end most of the lawsuits against glyphosate and avert possible legal risks in the future.
According to the Bayer side, after a settlement, 75 per cent of the current legal disputes over Roundup (Nanda) brand herbicides will be closed -- a total of approximately 125,000 cases, including lawsuits and uninitiated cases.
The rest will also be closed in the coming months.
For outstanding claims, Bayer paid a fixed amount of compensation, which was already included in the $10 billion.
Werner Baumann, the company's chairman, told German media NTV that this was done to better "look to the future" and "dispel unease" now.
"The settlement agreement was unanimously approved by the Bayer Board of Directors and the Board of Supervisors with the participation of a specialized committee on glyphosate law," Bayer said.
However, in the agreement, Bayer did not admit at all fault or misconduct.
The expensive Monsanto legacy In 2018, Bayer, a Dax company based in Leverkusen, Germany, bought American agrochemical giant Monsanto at a high price of more than $60 billion. Monsanto produces herbicides containing glyphosate, including a herbicide named Roundup, as well as Dicamba and PCB herbicides, which are suspected of carcinogenic.
After Bayer was convicted in three lawsuits of paying hefty compensation, more and more people sued the company, claiming to have developed cancer by using Monsanto's herbicide.
The indictments are based largely on a 2015 assessment by the WHO's Cancer Research Agency (IARC).
Unlike other institutions, IARC assessed glyphosate as "potentially carcinogenic".
Bayer dismissed the accusations and, in the near future, received support from the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which found that there was no health risk when glyphosate was used as instructed.
However, Bayer has now decided to accept the settlement, claiming that the final cost of the marathon, considering the pending outcome in the United States, may be higher.
At a video news conference with the media, Bayer Chairman Bob Bowman said he hoped to look forward and pay more attention to the company's core business.
He also said the settlement would not have an impact on Bayer's products and on future decisions on whether to use glyphosate.
In addition, Bayer announced that an independent "scientific committee" would be established for possible future "herbicide" cases, which would assess whether and at what dose Roundup might trigger lymphoma.
The wave of lawsuits to pay for herbicides this year has put Bayer under heavy pressure on the stock market, as well as criticism from corporate management, headed by chairman Werner Baumann.
Financially, Bayer can afford the cost.
The sale of the animal medicine sector alone would generate $7.6 billion in revenue for Bayer, most of which is paid in cash and a small share of Elanco's shares.
The Bears plan to start paying out this year.
Investors were divided on the news that Bayer had reached a settlement.
On the trading platform Tradegate, Bayer rose by nearly 9% at first, and did not perform much in conventional trading, eventually closing down.
One shareholder said it was a typical “sell on good news ” that investors had recently been signalled that a settlement should be reached and sold after the boots had landed.

Content: By 2100, the summer in Russia and other countries of the Northern Hemisphere will last up to six months, if we do not take measures to mitigate the effects of climate change.
This conclusion was reached by researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Phys.org.
According to scientists, climate change will have far-reaching negative effects on agriculture, human health and the environment.
Scientists analyzed daily climate data from 1952 to 2011 in the Northern Hemisphere.
The study showed that the duration of the summer increased from 78 to 95 days on average, and the duration of the winter decreased from 76 to 73 days.
Spring and autumn also decreased from 124 to 115 days and from 87 to 82 days respectively.
Accordingly, spring and summer began earlier, and autumn and winter - later.
The Mediterranean region and the Tibetan Highlands have experienced the greatest changes in their seasonal cycles.
If these trends persist without any efforts to mitigate climate change, researchers predict that the winter in the Northern Hemisphere will last less than two months by 2100, the transitional spring and autumn seasons will also decrease.
This in turn will have a strong impact on agriculture, human health and the environment, researchers warn.
Thus, the routes and timing of migration of birds will change, the plants will bloom in an uncharacteristic period.
These changes can lead to great disturbances in natural communities, scientists say.
In addition, they believe that with a longer growing season, people will inhale more pollen, causing allergies, and mosquitoes carriers of diseases will expand their habitat to the north.
Seasonal changes can also damage agriculture, researchers believe.
Moreover, such seasonal shifts can cause devastating weather events.
"A hotter and longer summer threatens to increase waves of abnormal heat and the occurrence of forest fires throughout the planet.
In addition, warmer and shorter winters can cause instability that will lead to cold waves and winter storms similar to the recent weather collapse in Texas, ” said Tsongwen Zhu, a monsoon researcher at the Climate System Institute of the China Academy of Meteorological Sciences.
Moscow, Natalia Petrova Moscow.

Title: Syngenta CEO: the company ’ s share in the Russian market is 4% and will grow

Content: Chief Executive Officer of Syngenta: the company 's share in the Russian market is 4% and will grow Eric Firvald told Interfax about the impact of the US trade war with China, production in Russia and "green" technologies Chief Executive Officer of Syngenta Eric Firvald Photo: Anatoly Medvedev / TASS Moscow.
October 11.
INTERFAX.RU - The agricultural sector is increasingly in the focus of the world market, both in connection with the trade conflict between the United States and China, in which the purchase of American agricultural products is one of the main advantages of Beijing, and in connection with climate change issues.
Erik Firvald, Chief Executive Officer of the Swiss-Chinese company Syngenta, the largest supplier of plant and seed protection products in Russia, gave his opinion on international problems, as well as on the prospects of the Russian market in an interview with Interfax. - When the Chinese ChemChina acquired Syngenta in 2017, it was said that the company will return to the exchange within five years, subject to a favorable market situation.
How do you assess the current market conditions, is there any preparation for IPO? - Preparation is under way.
I assess the current market situation as challenging, especially this year due to floods in the US and drought in Australia.
However, the situation in Russia is relatively good.
Preparation for IPO is under way.
We plan to continue the preparatory activities next year and hold the placement by 2022, while the market conditions are favorable, and the company shows solid results. - Given that you are an American, leading a Chinese company, how will you appreciate the latest events of the US trade war with China? - Syngenta and the entire industry generally supports open trade.
We believe that the less trade barriers, the better for all, for consumers and for the growth of the world economy.
It is a pity that China and the United States are in a state of trade war, and we hope that it will soon end.
As a result of the trade conflict, American farmers have essentially lost access to the huge Chinese market, now they have to either stockpile their products or sell them to other countries.
Some agricultural products from the United States were recently supplied to Brazil, where they were used as forage, and Brazil supplied its goods to China.
This entails additional logistics costs and reduced market efficiency.
In addition, the US is our largest market, and we are frustrated by the current state of affairs.
The Syngenta position is that the trade conflict is not a disastrous factor, but we hope that it will be resolved. - Tell us more about the situation in Russia.
- First, I would like to note the efforts of the Russian Government, Russian farmers and the industry as a whole, which have made it possible to significantly increase not only the country's self-sufficiency in agricultural production, but also the export growth.
The production volumes of many crops are increasing.
Syngenta has played a role in this success by providing its products, technologies, and scientific support.
This year our business in Russia demonstrates growth, which allows us to increase investments in the Russian market, thereby demonstrating support for the agricultural sector and confidence in the future of the sector.
We expect that the growth rate of our business in Russia this year will be measured by an unambiguous figure in the range from medium to high.
This is higher than the average in the world. - By investment, do you mean plans to build a plant in the Lipetsk region, or do you have other large projects? - In addition to this project, we create the Seed Protection Institute to provide the Russian market with the latest developments in this field, allowing to significantly increase yields.
We are also expanding our efforts in the field of seed production. - The two most important businesses for Syngenta are the production of seeds and plant protection products.
Two years ago, you said that in the world, the company ranks first in the segment of the CSR and the third in the production of seeds, which you intend to strengthen.
How far have you managed to do this? - In addition to organic growth, which is faster than the average market, we have made a number of acquisitions, including the purchase of Nidera Seeds, which has become the largest deal in the history of Syngenta.
Nidera is a leader in the production of soybean and corn seeds in Brazil and Argentina.
In addition, we have acquired the American company Abbott & Cobb, which is engaged in the production of seeds of vegetable crops and, in particular, sugar corn.
Thanks to these and other acquisitions, we have strengthened our third position in the segment of seed production and remain the world leader in the production of CDS.
In Russia, we occupy the first place in both segments. - What is the share of each segment in your revenue? - In Russia, seeds account for about 40% of sales, the SPR - about 60%. - How important is the Russian market for the company as a whole? - Russia accounts for just under 4% of the total revenue of Syngenta.
Our business in Russia demonstrates good growth rates, and it is very important for the company as a whole.
We expect that the share of the Russian market in our sales will increase in the future. - In what directions do you see the main opportunities for growth? - The production of corn is growing actively, and taking into account climate change, corn can now be grown in the more northern regions, up to the Moscow region, where previously this culture did not grow.
Climate change is a major global challenge that also offers new opportunities, as in the example of maize.
Climate change is also fraught with droughts, especially in the southern regions, and in response, we have developed a more arid maize variety.
This is how we help farmers overcome the challenges posed by climate change.
We also have digital solutions for farmers, and they are actively gaining popularity.
We have an application that contains satellite imagery of agricultural land all over the world.
For example, in the US, where the most severe flooding in history happened this year, farmers can see from the pictures which areas of water have already left, and begin to sow these areas in the first place.
We also offer weather risk insurance to Russian clients.
That is, customers purchase our seeds, and in case of emergency weather conditions, we reimburse them a part of the costs.
In 2018, 31 Russian agricultural companies took part in the program, including the largest agricultural holdings - "Miratorg" and "Ekoniva".
On the part of insurance companies, our partner is Japanese Sompo Japan. - Do you see increased competition from Russian seed producers and CSR? - Competition from Russian companies has always been strong, and I do not see any changes in this regard.
Our advantage lies in the international experience, through which we help local agricultural companies understand the demands of the world market with a focus on exports, including to China. - What share of the products sold in Russia you now produce in our country, and what are the successes of Syngenta on the way to the goal - to produce in the Russian Federation 80% of the products sold in the local market? - There is progress, and we will fulfill our commitment to bring the level of localization of plant protection products to 80% by 2021.
Currently, the share of seeds produced in Russia is 35-40% of sales, SZR - a little more, and after the opening of a new plant in the Lipetsk region, the indicator will grow even stronger.
It is worth noting that, moving towards this goal, we pay special attention to maintaining the highest quality standards in Russian production. - And in the future you are considering the possibility of exporting your products in Russia? - Everything is possible, and if we have free capacities, we will consider the issue of exports.
First of all, this will apply to the EAEU countries.
However, the factory in Lipetsk is first of all aimed at satisfying the demand in the Russian market. - Where else do you produce your products in Russia? - In the field of CSR it is Kirovo-Chepetsk.
The construction of the plant in the Lipetsk region will begin within a few weeks, and we will continue to use the capacities of our partner in Kirovo-Chepetsk.
In terms of seeds, we produce our own hybrids in Russia.
But I would like to note that in Russia, it takes about five years to approve a new hybrid variety, which is two years longer than in the rest of the world.
Therefore, I believe that we need to work together with other companies in the industry and with government officials to accelerate hybrid production while maintaining strict regulatory requirements.
Thus, we will maintain Russia ’ s competitive position in comparison with other countries.
In addition, in order for Russia to maintain a leading position in the world agricultural market, it is necessary to establish clear and scientifically sound rules for new technologies - such as genome editing.
This technology is supported by the authorities of the United States, Brazil, Canada, China.
Europe does not yet know what to do with this technology - there is talk that it can be equated with GMOs and, accordingly, abandon it.
In this case, the technology can significantly accelerate natural selection processes without the use of third-party DNA.
We call on the Russian government to consider developing regulations for genome editing technology in order to strengthen the competitive advantage. - Is there a demand in Russia for "green" technologies? - We observe such a demand.
It is smaller than in Western Europe, but there is no doubt that demand exists.
This applies not only to producers, but also to consumers.
Interest in environmental issues is growing, and we see it, communicating with the authorities, with our customers.
Russia is no different from other regions.
In my opinion, Russia ’ s desire to increase agricultural exports will also result in a desire to make production more environmentally friendly, because importing countries are increasingly demanding this.
In this I see a huge opportunity for Russia, and Syngenta is ready to help.
In the world, CO2 emissions are important for many large companies that purchase agricultural products.
In particular, it is Kellogg, which points to its products the volume of greenhouse gas emissions in their production and accordingly prefers low emission producers.
Thus, by reducing emissions and producing environmentally friendly products, farmers are able to increase profits.
Consumers increasingly want to know where their food was grown and how, and this trend carries huge opportunities for the agricultural sector. - What do you say about the increased demand for organic agricultural products, in the production of which no pesticides are used, which form an important part of your business? - This is not true.
Organic products manufacturers use a lot of pesticides, and many of them are our customers.
Unfortunately, there is a misconception, partly due to the lack of transparency on the part of manufacturers, that organic products are grown without pesticides.
In fact, they often use much more pesticides because their production is less efficient.
In doing so, organic agriculture has a negative impact on climate change.
It yields 35-40% less yields, and therefore requires more land on which trees could grow.
Organic land cultivation technologies, including the release of CO2 from the soil into the atmosphere.
From an environmental point of view, this is not very good, but consumers like the feeling that they buy "natural" products, and we understand that.
We believe that the right solution will be the effective use of technologies for safe cultivation of products that are healthy, of high quality and reduce the impact of the agricultural industry on climate change.
Agriculture and the food industry account for 25 per cent of the world's greenhouse gas emissions, and, given the population growth, increasing organic farming will only aggravate the situation.
We need to find a way to get a larger harvest from a smaller area, while using fewer pesticides of higher quality.
By the way, due to the improvement of the quality of pesticides, the amount of application of plant protection products per hectare of arable land has decreased by 95% over the past 50 years.
In Italy, for example, there is a high demand for organic products, and therefore farmers use copper-based drugs - and I do not think that huge amounts of copper poured on the soil are better than a small amount of modern synthetic pesticides.
In New Zealand, the largest producer of apples has drastically reduced the volume of organic production due to the use of very large volumes of pesticides.
And this year in Austria was completely destroyed the harvest of organic potatoes due to phytofluorosis.
Syngenta highlights three main areas in which the company can best help to stop or slow down climate change.
This is an increase in yields, so that farmers use less land while increasing production, improving tillage technologies to prevent CO2 from being released into the atmosphere, and restoring unsuitable land.

Content: In July of last year, the capital of Yemen, Sana, was attacked by a cloud of locusts on July 27, a cloud of grasshoppers covered Las Vegas, finding themselves in the center of the news that flew around the world.
They came from the desert, attracted by the lights of the big city.
At the same time, a cloud of insects invaded Yemen, a State devastated by civil war and suffering from food shortages.
The second invasion was less interesting to the media, although it had much more alarming consequences: it was locust, whose famous greed could cause significant crop damage in more than 60 countries, mainly in Africa, the Middle East and Central Asia.
These two episodes, at first glance quite different, are, in the opinion of some researchers, links of the same chain and threaten to become a frequent phenomenon: scientists warn that global warming entails changes in the behavior of insects, which become more dangerous and less predictable.
Hunger is not an aunt Scientists already have evidence that an increase in temperature in the atmosphere entails changes in the metabolism of insects.
In 2018, a group of American researchers published an article in the journal Science, which states that the warmer around, the more active the reproductive function of insects, and the better their appetite.
So, a desert locust consumes in a day the amount of food equal to its own weight.

Title: How climate change in Uzbekistan is assessed

Content: Since 2014, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has been the warmest ever observed year since then.
Most likely, 2019 will not be an exception to this alarming trend.
This July rewrote the history of climate, setting dozens of new temperature records at the local, national and global levels, WMO Secretary General Petteri Taalas said.
Uzbekistan is among the countries most vulnerable to climate change.
Since 1880, the average annual temperature in the country has risen by 1.6 degrees Celsius (from 13.2 to 14.8 degrees), which exceeds the average growth rate on the planet.
Air temperatures in the Central Asian region are projected to increase by a further 1.5 to 3 degrees between 2030 and 2050.
Here, the largest increase in air temperature is expected in the Aral Sea, because due to the drying of the Aral Sea, there are also specific local climatic changes.
As assessed by climate change, Uzbekistan has been a party to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) since 1993 and ratified the Paris Climate Agreement in 2018.
The country has made voluntary quantitative commitments to reduce the carbon intensity of GDP (greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP) and to adapt to climate change.
Uzhydromet under the Ministry of Emergency Situations is a responsible organization for fulfilling the obligations under the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement.
Earlier, Uzhydromet prepared the first (1999), second (2008) and third national communications on climate change (2016).
The Paris Agreement requires a country to maintain: reports on inventories of sources of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and assessment of the impact of mitigation measures every two years; national climate change reports every four years.
inventory of sources of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions.
Since 2019, the preparation of the fourth national communication, which will take about two years, reported to Gazeta.uz Uzgidromet expert Raisa Taryannikova, who participated in the preparation of the third national communication.
As a result, the first biennial report on the inventory and impact assessment of mitigation measures and the inventory of greenhouse gas emissions sources for 1990 - 2018 are also to be prepared in 2021.
Where and how should these data be used?
The most vulnerable agriculture gives people food.
And it is most sensitive to climate change, noted the expert of UZGIP ("Uzgipromeliovodkhoz") Tatyana Khamzina at a training for journalists on September 10, organized by the Regional Environmental Center of Central Asia.
The agricultural sector accounts for 27% of employment in the country, and the livelihood of rural residents is mainly dependent on agricultural production, the expert said.
Increasing heat supply during climate warming can bring benefits to agriculture - for example, wintering of animals will be easier, less need to cover heat-loving crops for the winter, may increase the sugar content of grapes.
There are increasing opportunities for obtaining several crops per year, growing late ripe and heat-loving crops — but these benefits will be real only with sufficient moisture supply, said Tatyana Khamzina.
However, there are increasing problems with water supply: according to World Bank estimates, the need for water for irrigation in agriculture has not been fully met.
Due to lack of water, winter wheat, cotton and orchards can be expected to decline by 7 - 9%, 4 - 5%, 6 - 8%, respectively, by 2030.
The World Bank estimates that the whole strategy to replace fragmented solutions to climate change damage to the economies of Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Kyrgyzstan ranges from 0.4% to 1.3% of their annual GDP.
In Uzbekistan, too, it is necessary to analyze the possible damage to the main sectors of the economy - water supply, energy, agriculture and forestry, transport - from climate change, the expert of the World Bank Benoit Boske "Gazet.uz" said.
A number of state programs are devoted to the Aral Sea to mitigate the consequences of the Aral disaster and the development of the region; documents have been adopted on the development of agriculture, irrigation, improvement of land reclamation and use of water resources.
At the same time, a World Bank expert notes the fragility of this work, as there is no “single national coordination mechanism to respond effectively to the challenges of climate change ”.
Indeed, the country does not yet have a comprehensive climate change response strategy that requires that these changes be taken into account in the adoption and implementation of all State-wide and sectoral development programmes and plans.
The development of an agricultural development strategy for the next 10 years has recently been initiated, which will largely reflect the responses to climate challenges.
One of the main directions of the strategy is the improvement of efficiency and maintenance of accounting for water use, as well as the introduction of water-saving technologies on 200 thousand hectares of land each year.
“200 thousand hectares each year on water-saving technologies is a very ambitious task.
But if we do not set such ambitious goals, there will be no progress, - said Alexey Volkov, the national coordinator of the Global Environment Facility (GEF SGP) Small Grants Programme, Gazeta.uz. - We hope that the GEF SGP experience in soil protection agriculture will be reflected in the draft of this strategy. "

Anna Nikolaeva and Maria Shalaeva Yura Borisov and Anna Shevchuk Natasha Merkulova and Alexey Chupov Ilya Bachurin Philip AvdeevThe choice of the program director of the festival Stas Tyrkin on the picture of Rasuloff as the final screenings on the “Strelka ” fell not accidentally.
At the Berlin Film Festival, the last screening before the global pandemic, the film received the Golden Bear, the main award.
The picture itself consists of four novels, which tell about the inhabitants of modern Iran.
The hero of the first of them is the man Hishmat, who lives in Tehran, who spends his day in ordinary household chores: cooks lunch, takes her daughter from school, visits her mother and helps her wife.
All this in the day, at night Hishmat starts to work in the night shift - and here what is a routine for him, turns into a tragedy for others and a shock for viewers.
The other three stories in “Evil does not exist ” also explore the paradoxes of life in modern Iranian society, and in one of the novels, the daughter of director Baran Rasulof starred.
By the way, she received a reward in Berlin instead of her father: because of the conflict with the Iranian authorities, Mohammad himself could not attend the festival.
