Content: SpaceX launches the Crew Dragon Resilience spacecraft.
The first in the history of SpaceX, as well as in the history of space technology, the flight of four astronauts aboard the Crew Dragon as part of the Crew-1 mission is about to begin.
We tell you everything you need to know about the mission.
Preparations for the flight took place especially actively.
Engineers and technical specialists pre-checked the readiness of all systems, Channel 24 reports.
Do not miss SpaceX received NASA 's first ever license for manned flights Crew-1 Stream NASA Stream SpaceX Stream All you need to know about the flight. Unlike the historic Demo-2 mission, the purpose of which was to demonstrate the technical ability of delivering people to the ISS with the help of the Crew Dragon, the Crew-1 mission is the first full-fledged NASA and Space-manned mission. eX.
As part of the mission, the first international crew of four astronauts for Crew Dragon will go to ISS: Michael Hopkins, Shannon Walker, Victor Glover and Japanese Soichi Noguchi.
Crew-1 astronauts mission inside the Crew Dragon Resilience crew The crew is NASA astronaut Michael Hopkins.
He's not new in orbit, and he's already been to the ISS, where he spent 166 days.
Of these, Hopkins spent 12 hours and 58 minutes outside the station while performing tasks that required access to outer space.
The pilot of Crew Dragon is astronaut Victor Glover, who joined NASA in 2013, and in 2017 he was selected as a pilot for the Crew-1 mission.
Mission specialist Shannon Walker is an experienced astronaut who joined NASA in 2004 and flew on shuttles to the ISS.
The Crew-1 mission for Walker will be the second flight into orbit.
Mission specialist Soichi Noguchi is a Japanese veteran astronaut who has been in JAXA since 1996.
He is the only on the team and the third astronaut in history to fly into space on three different ships: the shuttle, the Soyuz and the Crew Dragon.
Mission specialists are tasked with supporting the commander and pilot during the flight.
They monitor the state of the systems at startup and return, and are responsible for the working schedule, telemetry and inventory on the ship.
As Crew Dragon flies with four people on board for the first time, mission experts will help determine how to better organize and distribute tasks in such conditions.
The Crew-1 mission team is preparing to take seats in the Crew Dragon ship, video: Take a peek at the crew making their way through the crew access arm and adding their signatures to "the white room."
# LaunchAmerica pic.twitter.com / nySGwC47H0 — NASA (@ NASA) November 15, 2020 Flight plan Under favorable weather conditions, the rocket starts on November 16 at 2: 27 Kyiv time.
The ship will reach the ISS on November 17 at 06: 00 in Kiev and in offline mode is joined with the node IDA-2 module "Harmony".
Manual docking mode is also provided in case of emergency situation.

It is worth noting that after that the ISS crew will increase to 7 people, and this is the first time in almost ten years, when there will be more than six people in orbit on the ISS.
By the way, the station has only six beds: four in the American segment of the station and two in the Russian, which means that someone will have to sleep on the ship Crew Dragon.
Captain Michael Hopkins is likely to take a seat in the ship, according to the old tradition of astronauts since the shuttle flight.
Subsequently, another cabin will be delivered to the ISS.
In general, the Crew-1 mission will last five and a half months.
All this time astronauts will spend on research, experiments and work to maintain the station, including the launch into outer space.
Interestingly, as part of one of the tasks, astronauts will have to "repark" the Crew Dragon ship from the IDA-2 docking node to IDA-3.
This will happen in early 2021 – before the arrival of the Boeing Starliner, which will have to dock to the IDA-2.
The return to Earth is scheduled for spring 2021.
By this, Crew-1 will probably have time to cross with Crew-2, so there is every chance to see two Crew Dragon ships at the station at once.
Interesting fact.
The launch of the Crew Dragon was previously scheduled for November 15, but was delayed due to unfavorable weather conditions that prevented the floating platform Just Read The Instructions from reaching the landing zone in time.
This is an important point, as NASA expects to reuse the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket at the launch of the Crew-2 mission.
The updated Crew Dragon Ship, on which the Crew-1 mission team will go to the ISS, has received some changes compared to the previous version.
The fact is that during the flight of the Demo-2 mission, it turned out that several heat-shielding tiles were more degraded than expected.
SpaceX noted that this did not threaten the crew.
The problem was solved by replacing the necessary heat protection plates with a more stable version.
In addition, experts replaced the atmospheric pressure sensor on the ship, which is used to determine the height.
Last time the parachutes were opened a little later than expected by the technicians (but within the norm).
Finally, the new Dragon capsule of the Crew-1 mission was named Resilience.
The crew dedicated this name to the staff of SpaceX, NASA, their loved ones and all the people who are resilient during the global pandemic.

Title: NASA: Manned Dragon spacecraft to be launched on US soil on Wednesday

Content: On May 27, two astronauts from NASA, Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley, will fly from the United States to space.
This is the first time in nine years that American astronauts have flown to the International Space Station (ISS) without having to travel to Kazakhstan aboard a Russian rocket.
NASA announced Saturday that the two astronauts will travel to the International Space Station aboard the SpaceX spacecraft Crew Dragon.
This is part of NASA's Commercial Manned Aviation Program (CCP).
The Falcon 9 rocket carrying the manned Dragon spacecraft will be launched Wednesday at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The mission, which will be the final test of the manned Dragon spacecraft, will be used to validate the manned spaceflight system, including launch pads, rockets, spacecraft and operational capabilities, NASA said.
After successful trials, the CPP will certify that the manned Dragon spacecraft has long-term operational capability for the International Space Station.
NASA said the certification would allow them to "continue their important research and technical missions" on the International Space Station for the benefit of mankind.
Both Becken and Haley were selected for this role because of their extensive space experience.
They carried out multiple space missions before 2011.
After successful docking, the two astronauts will become members of the Expedition 63 crew of the International Space Station and assist in testing the manned Dragon spacecraft.
In addition, they will carry out other studies with the staff of the International Space Station.
Watch the video 01: 17 Share the Cosmic Red Mask Send Facebook google + Whatsapp Tumblr Weibo Double Kaixin Digg Newsvine Fixed link https: / / p.dw.com / p / 32sRd Cosmic Red Mask NASA says manned Dragon spacecraft can stay on the International Space Station for about 110 days, but the specific mission duration will be determined based on the launch readiness of the next commercial crew.
After the mission, the manned Dragon spacecraft will take two astronauts to the space station and re-enter the Earth's atmosphere.
NASA said the mission "laid the groundwork for future exploration of the Moon and Mars."
According to the Agency's Artemis program, humans will return to the moon in 2024, including a female astronaut, which will be the first female lunar landing.

Title: Ukraine airliner shot down Iran claims accidental UN investigators lied – Radio France Internationale

Content: A Ukrainian airliner was shot down near Tehran last year at the height of tension between Iran and the United States, United Nations officials said today, accusing the Iranian government of lying about the cause of the crash.
On January 8, 2020, Ukraine International Airlines Flight PS752 crashed shortly after taking off from Tehran, Iran, killing all 176 people on board, including 55 Canadian citizens.
Three days later, Iran admitted that its troops fired two missiles and accidentally shot down the Boeing 737-800, which was scheduled to fly to Kiev, Ukraine.
The United Nations Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial executions, Agnes Callamard, published the findings of the tragedy, stating that the explanations provided by the Iranian Government were contradictory.
"What is most troubling is that the Iranian authorities are totally unreasonable about the mistakes made, whether by single fault or multiple mistakes," she told reporters.
She said Iran's interpretation of the crash was "contradictory, contrary to the facts and inconsistent with the technical assessments made by many experts."
Karamalde said, "There really is no other way to say that Iran is lying, but why are they doing this?"
Karamalde said Iran could not explain how the military had made such a serious mistake in shooting down a passenger plane.
Karamalde said that "miskilling" is possible under international law, and the Law Society decides whether the fault was committed in good faith or not.
"I concluded that, on the basis of international law, Iran cannot justify its failure," Karamalde said, adding that relations between Iran and the United States were strained when Ukrainian International Airlines Flight PS752 was shot down.

Title: Why Russia tolerates DPRK ’ s antics

Content: The Russian team of the Seiner "Xianhailin-8" has been held by North Korea for more than a week, but it became known only the day before.
The Embassy of the Russian Federation in the DPRK worked on the release of sailors, trying not to raise the noise, but the scandalous story still leaked in the media.
Why do we have to tolerate such behaviour from a country that lives, including our humanitarian assistance?
The Russian seiner "Xianhailin-8" with a team of 17 people and a crab catch on board went to the Russian port of Zarubino, from where the cargo was intended to be transported to the South Korean city of Sokcho, but on the night of 16 to 17 July was detained by border guards of the DPRK.
The detention was obviously illegal, as it occurred at a distance of 53 nautical miles from the shores of North Korea.
Territorial waters, according to the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, are 12 miles from the shore.
The Democratic People's Republic of Korea believes that the Convention is not a decree, and attempts to control a zone 50 miles from the shore, which it does not always succeed.
Seiner, again, was arrested when he was 53 miles away.
Currently, the ship is held in the port of Wonsan, most of the Russian sailors - prisoners of their cabins.
The exception is made only for the captain, his assistant and two South Korean sailors - they were placed in the hotel.
According to Victor Sedler, the director of the North-East Fishing Company, which owns the Seiner, the main problem is the temperature in the cabins, which rises to 35 degrees.
Russian sailors are not allowed to go to the deck, are interrogated and searched daily, there was a risk that they would run out of food and water.
Representatives of the Russian embassy met with the sailors before the news of their detention spread to the media.
According to the diplomatic mission's press release, the detainees are healthy.
At the same time, “all necessary measures shall be taken to resolve the situation as soon as possible ”.
There is reason to believe that optimism in this case is not unfounded, that soon sailors will be released, and the seiner will be sent to the Russian port.
In favor of this says at least a comment of an employee of the Embassy of the DPRK in Moscow, as if by the way mentioned about "good relations" between Moscow and Pyongyang.
“Before that, our vessels have been detained in the DPRK on numerous occasions, often enough.
And in general, the consequences have never been severe.
It took some time, we considered and let go, - said the President of the Far Eastern Association of Marine Captains Peter Osichansky to the VZLOAD newspaper. - Perhaps there will be a fine for sailors and shipowner, no more than that.
Most likely, sailors accidentally got into these waters.
If no crime is established, a maximum of two weeks and a ship with sailors will be released. ”
Despite all this, the question is in the air - why does Russia tolerate such antics from the DPRK at all?
On this topic, let ’ s start with the fact that the antics of the DPRK are largely forced to endure everything.
And self-indulgence on the part of North Korean border guards is not the biggest problem yet.
The issues with North Korea's missile and nuclear programs are far more serious, but the "Juche regime" can be seen as a clear example of a truly independent foreign policy when "I want to do what I do."
In fact, the ideology of the Chuche implies this - identity and self-reliance based on the army (which in the DPRK as a percentage of the population as a whole - the largest on the planet).
Ultimately, we are dealing with a closed, unpredictable and extremely sovereign country, which has proven more than once that it is capable of surviving by blackmailing literally the entire world.
When Russia and China are accused in the West of being North Korea ’ s “lawyers ”, this is not true.
Both Beijing and Moscow regularly subscribe to international sanctions imposed on Pyongyang: as official members of the "nuclear club" and neighbors of the DPRK, by definition, we cannot be satisfied with the violation of the nuclear non-proliferation regime and missile testing near our borders, especially since the manageability of Korean missile crafts is questionable.
In view of this, even the relations between Pyongyang and Beijing in recent years are regarded by experts as "cool", although the PRC is perceived in the DPRK as the only real ally.
Beijing and Moscow are the best countries to understand who they are dealing with and see as their main task the reduction of tension in the region.
Truly hard pressure on Pyongyang can dangerously aggravate the situation, and a full-fledged war (in the future, we remind you, nuclear) would be catastrophic at all.
In such a situation, our only advantage is the “good relationship ” with the“ Juche regime ”, which is often called “special ”.
With the Russians and the Chinese, the North Koreans are at least ready to keep in touch, talk and negotiate.
It may seem funny, but it is true: the very opportunity to call Pyongyang to solve any issues is a luxury that few have.
And we appreciate this opportunity, because without it the situation will become much more dangerous.
As such problems are trying to solve in the United States, it is known that damage to all other parties will not be considered there.
Ultimately, the Russians and the Chinese periodically have to put aside their own pride and assume that the main thing is the positive resolution of important issues for us and the avoidance of open conflicts, not the approach that dictates the ambitions of the great Power.
Of course, it is possible to demand the release of Xianhailin-8 within three hours, threatening Pyongyang with “decisive measures ” and the armed forces, but the development of such a scenario is unpredictable in terms of the fate of our sailors and is frankly harmful in terms of maintaining the very possibility of dialogue with the DPRK.
That is why we “tolerate ”.
Even as the situation looks humiliating to us.
By the way, Russia has not just “good relations ” with the DPRK - we are the main supplier of humanitarian assistance to this country.
Despite this, our sailors are kept in cabins, and two South Koreans are accommodated in a hotel, although formally two Koreas are in a state of war.
It is worth admitting that our country has never been able to benefit from “special relations ” with the Kim dynasty regime, and the dialogue with the most closed society of the planet was a“ ceiling ” for us.
But the very appearance of the DPRK on the map is the all-round merit of our country.
Lee Seung Man and Kim Il Sung (photo: Public Domain) As you know, two parts of the once united Korea are two zones of occupation, Soviet and American, that is, the DPRK and RK - a kind of analogue of the GDR and Germany in Asia.
The difference is that at the time of the occupation of the USSR from the north and the United States from the south at the end of the Second World War, Korea was a Japanese colony, which, after the victory, was intended to grant independence as a single power.
The governments of Kim Il Sung in the North and Lee Seung Man in the South wanted to unite the country under their leadership and were going to fight for it.
The Nords formally began, but Joseph Stalin ’ s personal “good ” Kim Il Sung did not receive it immediately and only after he convinced Moscow that the US would not intervene in the conflict, and it would end very quickly because of the superiority of the North over the South in terms of armaments (which, of course, was also the merit of Moscow).
The US is known to have intervened, and the bloody war, in which Pyongyang passed twice from hand to hand, and Seoul four times, ended almost at the same place where it began.
The DPRK lost a little more territory than it acquired, though, and did not acquire anything, in the ancient capital of Korea, Kason.
The USSR did not acquire anything at all.
The rational format of participation in the Korean conflict, chosen by Stalin (pilots, senators, military advisers, but not the troops themselves), minimized our physical losses - the same Americans left more than 37,000 soldiers in Korea.
Even economic losses can not be said - we armed the Chinese army, which thoroughly entered the Korean war, not for free.
But that was what ultimately determined our geopolitical damage.
In Beijing, they were frankly offended by the fact that Moscow uses Chinese soldiers as "cannon meat" and refuses gratis military supplies.
This resentment was followed by a serious cooling of relations between the two countries and a military conflict on the island of Damansky.
On the contrary, the US was able to improve relations with Germany and Japan precisely against the background of the Korean war, which has become an occasion for the Western world to unite and militarize against the “red threat ”.
It could have ended a lot worse for everyone.
For example, United Nations commander General Douglas MacArthur (officially opposed to the DPRK by the United States, but by the United Nations coalition) advocated a nuclear strike on China's territory.
Thus, no one has ever been able to extract any real bonuses from the DPRK.
Communist China is no exception here either: if it were not for the Korean war, it might well have taken control of Taiwan.
For both Moscow and Beijing, North Korea has always been a source of problems and losses, a symbol of unrealized opportunities.
This situation is stable, as the “Juche regime ” itself is stable.
And all we have to do is keep an eye on how bad it may be.

Content: Ernest Hemingway, Nobel laureate and one of the most important of the 20th century, was born on July 21, 1899 in Illinois, and during his lifetime he wrote seven novels, six short stories, and two non-fiction books.
On the occasion of the author ’ s birthday, which coincided with July 31, we have some suggestions for better study of the author ’ s works.
Hemingway works are fluent, simple and clear, but for many literary audiences, the beginning of Hemingway books may be hard.
Why Hemingway?
Ernst Hemingway is an influential writer in the history of literature and fiction, and his works have often won the most prestigious international literary awards such as Nobel and Pulitzer, which employed a different type of fiction and led many of his subsequent writers to be lenders of his particular literary style.
Hemingway has called his literary style the Ice Berg theory, in this way of writing, narrative events such as a floating iceberg in water, only one eighth visible, and the author contains only information in the story that is essential in its process and eliminates the rest of the information.
This technique produced a dramatic transformation in storytelling, especially in writing short stories, and it was a transformation that freed stories from conventional rhetoric.
Hemingway ’ s works are included in the list of books of the century, books to read before death and the best fiction books of history, which shows the importance of this author.
What should we know?
One of the things that helps to better understand Ernest Hemingway's works is getting to know his personal life.
Many of the things we read in his books are the things he has turned from his personal life into a story.
At the age of 19, he volunteered for World War I, but was not allowed to fight due to visual impairments, but Hemingway was forced to serve as an ambulance driver for the Red Cross.
He was injured several times during Cheng, but his most important injury is when he was injured by mortar shells and stayed in the hospital for a long time, the novel Farewell to Arms is a narrative of this part of Hemingway and World War.
Even Catherine Barkley's character in the book was made up of the nurse Hemingway was fond of.
Hemingway also participated in World War II as a war correspondent, and several short stories are the result of this era.
The sun continues to blow, the great river or along the river to the trees, each of which is somehow tied to the World War, and their heroes are survivors of the war and have many memories of this time.
But Hemingway's most important masterpiece is a memento of his childhood, Hemingway's father had a great interest in fishing, and this hobby was also transferred to Ernest, which is clearly seen in the famous story of the old man and the sea.
But before the old man and the sea he had written Hemingway about having and not having the captain of a fisherman.

You can see, this book is a story of an American soldier in the Spanish Civil War who fights with combatants against General Franco, who also did this.
Another important thing, perhaps, was that the conversationalist in World War II led a French group against the Nazis, who was tried after the war for armed action but was never proven guilty of a crime.
The political and social history of the world in the years of Hemingway's life, his personal life, and the awareness of his contemporary writers, such as Scott Fitzgerald, who wrote to him, are points that help to understand his works.
Familiarity with the writers of Hemingway period helps to see the difference between him and his contemporaries better.
Hemingway is classic?
To read Hemingway ’ s works, we must note that he is not a classical writer with a different style of writing, he did not have a middle class with long margins and descriptions of classical literature, and his long novels are not omitted.
He was interested in summarizing and engaging the audience with the story, which is a feature of modern literature.
In general, Hemingway works are innovative, and even among modern works they have their own special creativity, but the value of this writer 's work has always been compared to the classics, and even classics enthusiasts have not been able to be indifferent to it.
In these works we have a cheerful and eloquent writer, a writer who was in and out with young people in middle age and was also a close friend with a group of hippies.
Hemingway is a realist writer but has always tried to keep his sense of humor.
Where to start?
To study the works of the conversationalist, the first and most important suggestion is the book of the old man and the sea.
The book, translated by Najaf Daryabandari, is published by Kharazmi Publishing on 222 pages.

These two books are always included in the list of works to be read or masterpieces of the 20th century.
If you are interested in short stories, you can also read the book Men Without Women, which is a collection of stories published in various magazines of this author.
The book was translated by Asadullah Amraee for Ofoq's publication on 222 pages.
Even if you are interested in writing, Hemingway can be a good teacher for you and read his talk series and learn very precise things.
The last book of the interview and other talks by Ernest Hemingway has been published by Houshang Jirani on 88 pages by Cheshmeh Publishing.
The final season of many critics saw Ernest Hemingway as the greatest writer of the 20th century.
His stories are an exploration of human life, suffering, and the meaning of living.
The most important feature of this author is the portrayal of the inner emotions of the human being, which makes his work readable for everyone in a book.
Who was Ernest Hemingway?
Ernest Hemingway was born on July 21, 1899 in Oak Park, Illinois, United States.
His father, Clarence, was a doctor, and his mother, Grace, was a piano and singing teacher.
Ernest spent the summers with his family in northern Michigan, where he found his passion for fishing.
After finishing high school, he worked in Kansas City for a time in 1917 as a reporter for Star's Chronicles.
During World War I, he volunteered for military service, but his eyesight weakened him, and he was arrested instead as a Red Cross ambulance driver near the Italian front.
On 8 July 1918, he was injured and spent months in the hospital.
In 1925, his first short series of stories, in our time, was published, which well articulated his particular style.
His memories of the time that followed his death in 1964 were published as The Variable Eid.
Ernest Hemingway was most of his life engaged in adventure.
From being wounded in Italy by 200 shrapnel from Austrian forces during World War I to participating in the front lines of the Spanish Civil War or traveling to Africa's wildlife to fishing and hunting wild animals and living in Cuba.
At last he said good bye to life to his hunting gun.

Content: Photo copyright a Image capture Hemingway was the spokesperson for "Lost Generation" Ernest Hemingway liked to be a war reporter, professional athlete, hunter or adventurous traveler.
He considered writing little to himself, but eventually became one of the greatest writers of the 20th century.
He received both the Nobel Prize and influenced many post-World War II writers.
Today Hemingway is one of the pillars of the modern world.
He ended his life fifty years ago.
Ernest Hemingway was born in 1899 in Oak Park, a town in the state of Illinois, North America.
His father was a doctor and had provided a good life for the family.
Ernest was playful at school and disliked homework, but he got good grades.
Hemingway became a journalist at the age of 18.
With a rebellious temperament that never calmed down, his heart was in the air of distant villages, and he found this "opportunity" in the war.
To the ambulance driver of the International Red Cross, in the last year of the "Great War", he traveled to Europe with American troops.
During the war he felt the horror of death with flesh and skin.
During the Austrian bombardment, the wounds were severe and he was hospitalized for several months.
At the hospital in Milan, more than 200 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body, and he had the habit of pulling small iron from his feet at leisure with a knife tip.
Hemingway was also a lover and was impatient for beautiful women.
She married four times in her life, among dozens of love stories.
He fell madly in love with his nurse in the hospital.
But a few months later, after the war ended, he returned to America and married another woman.
He was 22 years old and his first wife was 29 years old.
A decent, kind woman, who was "accidentally" in a good financial situation.
A spokesman for "Lost Generation" Hemingway went to Europe with his young wife in 1921 and joined a group of modernist writers in Paris who were gathered in the "capital of modern art": Scott Fitzgerald, John Dus Pasus, Ezra Pound and...
This generation was called Gertrude Stein "Lost Generation."
The children of this generation lost all hope and faith in the plains of the mud of war and no longer believed in anything.
Moral lessons and moral values and boastful "bourgeois civilization" were considered a bunch of deceitful lies.
Hemingway, who had started writing real reports and his first short stories, brought this anger and frustration to the paper in a new tone and language.
His stories, full of freshness and vitality, instilled the deep anger and sadness of this generation with a vivid and effective expression.
The novel "The Sun continues to blow" was a live account of this generation, seeking a comfort that was not found in the western cities.
The novel "Farewell to Arms", published in 1928, clearly expressed this frustration.
Here the narrator was not a regular ruler.
Someone was talking about the war, which he had cut himself, and which he still had the shrapnel in his body.
Now, in a statement free of emotion, he remembered: "I had seen nothing sacred, and the things that were proud had no honor, and the victims were like cattle and sheep in Chicago slaughterhouse – if they had not done anything with carcasses of meat except to bury them..."
(Farewell to Arms, translation of Najaf Daryabandari) This was the mass look of those who lost in the war anyway, and it was different, of course, from the look and expression of the Pharaohs and commanders, to whom the war was "the field of honor" and full of "blessings".
In this photo, Pauline Pfeiffer, his second wife, is seen. Some critics have made a point that taking part in the war for Hemingway was not only an experience that influenced his literary work, but, far beyond that, the whole war of his being and his mentality, gave him a "war-torn" mood. It shaped his worldview.
Hemingway was always ready to fight, and in everything he saw a challenge to fight and fight: in the field, in the boxing ring, or in the field of bullfights.
The novel "The Sun continues to blow", published in 1927, depicts this view in various diagrams and pictures of color.
In the "Death in the Afternoon" published in 1932 in the form of real memories or travelogues, the bull race is a metaphor for confronting death: to stand facing death, to look at it, to tremble at this horror / pleasure, to mix with it and finally to sink into its black palate.
They say that Hemingway's hobbies, fishing, hunting wild animals to hunting women, were examples of the constant temptation to fight and fight.
Even writing was a great challenge for him, and he went to the "crucifixion" with special discipline.
Some critics have said that he considered killing as the only natural form of human history, as far as he believed that "healthy and natural" should die in the field rather than in bed.
He was always a man of action and struggle in Hemingway Square.
He has got the means of his work, as he boasted, not from the works of others, but from blood and sweat.
Will Durant has said that, in a few writers, life experiences are intertwined with literary efforts such as bottleneck.
Hemingway hated intellectual habits and arguments.
He despised intellectuals who, absorbed in abstract arguments, had forgotten the principle of life; he called them cowards and uncourageous.
He was not a commentator, and did not even consider himself a literary and novelist, in the classical sense of it.
He once said, "I'm not going to compete with Talesto."
In his 1954 Nobel Prize speech, Hemingway explained his style with the metaphor "iceberg": "I try to be like the iceberg, with seven eighths hidden under the water and only one eighth visible.
The more we remove it from the body of the story, the stronger the iceberg becomes.
The power of the story is in things the writer knows but does not reveal.
If he omits something for not knowing, he is found in a hole in the story. "
The author knows all about his space and characters, but only gives the reader the least necessary information.
In this precise and measured and compact style, most of the incisions and explanations are removed, but do not disappear; the reader senses them and is more strongly affected.
With the "delete" technique, both in the story structure and in the language, a text provides a pure and clear, which has a direct and lightning effect.
The design or plot is invisible.
The language is compact, concise, dry, and sensational.
Cross and short sentences only pass a thin procedure and leave the rest to the reader ’ s intelligence.

I think it's quite typical how Ernest Hemingway defined a new regime in the country.
He said in Hemingway concise but expressive terms: “This is the first honest government in Cuba ’ s history, the first government to see its purpose in serving the people. ”
In the eyes of Hemingway, several Cuban governments have changed.
“All the former rulers, ” he says,“ did not have time to come to power, they began to use it to enrich themselves and their surroundings, even though it was nothing!
Napoleon and his marshals sought high standing by winning great battles, showing their talents and abilities.
And then some sergeant takes power, having no victories and no talent but knowledge of stenography. "
The writer meant Batista, who began his career as a staff writer.
We visited Hemingway at his house in the suburbs of Havana, where he has been spending most of his time for about twenty years.
One could expect a live classic to look solemn and serious.

Perhaps that is the peculiarity of true greatness?
Hemingway House stands on a hill surrounded by a small park with tall trees.

judgments.text: Sergo Mikoyan met Hemingway in Cuba, where Hemingway lived.

Title: FIGURE OF THE DAY. "Porcelain" history.21 July 2019

Content: July 21, 2019 THE WAR COMPETITION IS THE MOST RESPONSIBLE PEOPLE.
AND THAN NEXT TO THE ADVANCED, THEM ARE MORE OBSERVING PEOPLE THERE TO MEET.
WHO WANTS, FIGHTS AND WARS - LEGS THINKING ONLY ABOUT ECONOMIC COMPETITION AND THAT IT IS POSSIBLE TO CLICK ON IT... ''
These words were written long ago by Ernest Miller Hemingway, born exactly 120 years ago, on July 21, 1899, in the small American town of Oak Park, Illinois, in the family of a doctor.
He's been fond of hunting and fishing since he was a kid.
And I read a lot.
And he had one and only dream of becoming a writer.
And one day it came true.
He became a writer.
Not just a writer, a world-famous writer.
He wrote books that are familiar to every educated person.
Such as' 'Farewell, weapons' ',' 'And the sun rises (Fiesta)' ',' 'Whom the bell rings' ',' '' Death in the afternoon '', and many others.
His story "The Old Man and the Sea", written in 1952, won the Pulitzer Prize in 1953, and a year later won the Nobel Prize.
He fought in Italy.
He lived in Cuba.
He traveled through Africa.
He's been looking for himself all his life.
But I guess I never found it.
When Ernest was 12 years old, his grandfather gave him a 20-gauge single-charge gun.
He immediately rushed to the street to boast of a gift in front of friends from the poor outskirts of Chicago, where he lived with his parents at the time.
Seeing him, an old wise Indian woman said, "Be careful, boy.
These toys tend to go anywhere, including their owners... ''
She must have known what she said.
Exactly 50 years later, the world-famous writer Ernest Hemingway shot himself with the same gun.
This model was later called Hemingway.
Before that, fate had tested him many times.
Dozens of times he's been in the hairs of death.
One day in battle, he was hit by 273 shards of mines at once, and his legs pierced a machine-gun line!
But he survived.
He survived after five accidents and seven disasters.
Twice injured in the hunt and nearly burned during a forest fire...
I guess the old Indian woman knew something.
One time, Hemingway argued with fellow writers that he would write a six-word story in English, which would be the most touching of all his earlier writings.
They doubted.
And he took, and won this argument: '' For sale - baby shoes, never used... ''
('' Sold: baby shoes.
Unwanted... '').
After that, the world began to hold competitions for the shortest story, in which there would be a mandatory tie, culmination and isolation.
Here are just a few examples that have become widely known.
The chauffeur smoked and leaned over the gas tank to see if there was a lot of gas left.
The deceased was 23 years old. '' (O. Henry).
The last man on Earth sat in a room.
The door was knocked... ''
(Frederick Brown).
He was quite unpretentious in his life.
It was driven by the fact that one day he put on a clean sheet of paper: '' Now is not the time to think about what you don't have.
Think about how to handle what you have... ''
For many years, looking at the beautiful porcelain composition presented to you today, brought by me from Spain, I see in her main hero Ernest Hemingway.
For some reason, it seems to me that he was exactly like this...
May I wish all today's birthday children good and happiness.
And you, my friends, have a good day.
As always, truly yours.

judgments.text: Sergo Mikoyan characterized Hemingway's writing style as a combination of realism and romanticism.

Title: Pandora ’ s Box – Meeting with Hemingway

Content: A few days ago, Literary Newspaper turned 190 years old.
It was founded in 1830 with the participation of A.S. Pushkin, in 1929 the publication resumed with the assistance of A.M. Gorky.
The new breath and the new meaning of "Literary" gave... Stalin.
It was he who suggested adding volume and frequency to the newspaper.
This historical fact was described by Konstantin Simonov, and this scene entered my book Stalin.
We remember together. "
And now I want to bring to your attention the material from the jubilee issue of the Literary Newspaper, which published interesting materials of the past years.
Source: Literary newspaper Meeting with Hemingway In February 1960, the First Deputy Chairman of the USSR Council of Ministers, Anastas Mikoyan, visited the Republic of Cuba, where he arrived at the invitation of the Cuban Government to open the Exhibition of the achievements of the Soviet Union in the field of science, technology and culture.
On his trip to Cuba A.I. Mikoyan was accompanied by his son, journalist S. Mikoyan...
The Literary Newspaper publishes an excerpt from S. Mikoyan's essays describing Mikoyan's visit to writer Ernest Hemingway, who lives 12 kilometers from Havana, in San Francisco de Paula, and an excerpt from Hemingway's novel "3a River, in the Shadows of Trees".
I think it's quite typical how Ernest Hemingway defined a new regime in the country.
He said in Hemingway concise but expressive terms: “This is the first honest government in Cuba ’ s history, the first government to see its purpose in serving the people. ”
In the eyes of Hemingway, several Cuban governments have changed.
“All the former rulers, ” he says,“ did not have time to come to power, they began to use it to enrich themselves and their surroundings, even though it was nothing!
Napoleon and his marshals sought high standing by winning great battles, showing their talents and abilities.
And then some sergeant takes power, having no victories and no talent but knowledge of stenography. "
The writer meant Batista, who began his career as a staff writer.
We visited Hemingway at his house in the suburbs of Havana, where he has been spending most of his time for about twenty years.
One could expect a live classic to look solemn and serious.
However, he was rarely a direct, living, and cheerful person, who is somewhat ironic about what he is considered a great writer, and at least behaves not as great.
Perhaps that is the peculiarity of true greatness?
Hemingway House stands on a hill surrounded by a small park with tall trees.
There's an announcement on the gate that makes it clear that Hemingway rarely takes time to receive visitors.
Five to six rooms of this cozy house are full of sunlight, which freely penetrates through large windows.
There are many different hunting trophies in all rooms.
The writer's wife, Mary, an elderly woman with a young character, showed very clearly how she killed a huge lion in Africa.
The skin of this lion adorns the wall of one of the rooms.
There are several paintings in the living room and dining room.
Two or three - works of old masters.
I especially liked the two impressionist paintings depicting the bullfighting bullfighting.
A beautiful range of colors, matador and bull - in motion, in a desperate struggle not for life, but for death.
Unfortunately, I don't remember the name of the artist that the hostess called.
Mary Hemingway passionately loves painting and most of all in the house (except, perhaps, only the skin of the lion) is proud of his paintings. – The Art Gallery is the first thing I look at when I come to any capital: Paris or Madrid, London or Rome.
A.I. Mikoyan could not, of course, know this, but as if he had predicted by giving Mary Hemingway an album with reproductions of the paintings of the Leningrad Hermitage.
Hemingway's spouses were very interested in other gifts, such as the voice-over model of the satellite.
Especially amused their Russian folk toy handicrafts - matryoshka - five matryoshkas of different sizes, one in the other.
We brought the writer and the Russian vodka.
But I was surprised to see that among the bottles prepared for food is already exactly the same. - A few days ago, I learned that in Havana your composer Aram Khachaturyan, and invited him to his place.
I love his music very much.
And he himself, like his wife Nina Makarova, I really liked him.
They had lunch with us, we had a very interesting conversation.
Khachaturian left me this bottle of vodka.
And addressing the representative of the Union of Soviet Societies of Friendship and Cultural Relations with Foreign Countries Alexeev, who caught a cold and oghrip, Hemingway said: “And you do not know how to treat the throat?
I'll show you right now!
Bread vodka, he nearly for a minute rinsed her throat, bringing out complex rulades.
The writer showed us his job.
To a great surprise, we found that instead of the table, he was served by a small pyupiter standing by the wall in the bedroom.
By the way, a dozen and a half books were scattered on the bed.
Hemingway writes standing.
“In order not to sit back, ” he explained.
We went up to the tower that Mary Hemingway conceived and designed as her husband's workplace.
- I was thinking of saving him from the noise I make in the house - talk, dishes or a vacuum cleaner.
And what would you think?
He never works here.
We only climb the tower to admire the view of Havana.
You can see the sea on the other side.
Hemingway showed us his library.
The bookshelves are located in different rooms, including the famous tower.
A significant part of the books are his own works, translated into many languages and published in different countries.
To our surprise, from Russian editions he had only the story "The Old Man and the Sea", sent to him from the ship "Angara" by the Soviet writer N.N. Mikhailov.
N.N. Mikhailov turned out to be more attentive than those of our publishers who have recently published Hemingway ’ s books in large editions.
For example, shortly before our departure from Moscow, a two-volume book was released, which we had the pleasure of giving the author.
And on his return to Moscow, they sent him about two dozen of his books, published in various languages of the peoples of the USSR, and even the story "The Old Man and the Sea", published for the blind.
Cheerful and at the same time a little shy person, Hemingway does not like the official situation, ceremonies, honors, etc.
Never does anything that would prevent him from "getting up" for work every day at 6: 00 in the morning – up to 12 days.
A.I. Mikoyan asked Hemingway whether he intended to visit the Soviet Union, where he was so popular.
The writer replied: “I am sixty years old, and I cannot afford to delay the implementation of my plans.
I'm writing a new novel now.
I hope he will be no worse than Fiesta.
Until I finish it, I don't think I can interrupt.
But then I want to definitely visit your country.
By the way, the writer expressed his dissatisfaction with those American journalists who told the press that to the question whether he would go to the USSR, Hemingway replied negatively. "I, of course, could only accept for a joke the question whether I would go there with President Eisenhower, and answered them accordingly with a joke," he said.
My father introduced me to Hemingway, saying he could explain himself to me without an interpreter.
The writer asked if I really speak English. "A little," I said. "Like all of us," he immediately noticed, and it seemed to me that it was said quite seriously.
We started a conversation about the works of the writer, and in particular about the novel "Behind the River, in the Shadows of Trees", which has not yet been translated into Russian.
Hemingway wanted to give me this novel, the English edition of which was supposed to stand on one of the shelves, but it was not so easy to figure out the bookshelves, and he promised to send the book to Moscow...
The meeting with Hemingway was very friendly and direct, as if our acquaintance was a long time ago.
In a sunny cozy house all the time there was a lively conversation, a funny laugh sounded.
Already in Moscow, a few weeks after my return from Havana, I read in the newspaper “Worker ”, the organ of the Communist Party of the United States, the article“ Hemingway and the Revolution ”, which highly appreciates the writer ’ s work.
Hemingway, of course, is not a revolutionary.
But he is a great artist, a realist and at the same time a romantic.
The ability to brilliantly combine exciting romance (without which there are no revolutions) with real realism (which should explain why revolutions are taking place) and is apparently his individuality as a writer.
Getting acquainted with him, unwittingly find that the literary "me" of this modern classic fully meets the appearance of Hemingway himself - a sincere, sincere, just person with a gray beard, but with the youthful ability to get carried away and enjoy life, even if life pleases very few.
He could rightly say about himself: “I am a human being, and nothing human is alien to me. ”
He approaches social phenomena, perhaps with a few fuzzy ones, but, I would say, flawless positions for the non-revolutionary – from the point of view of humanism, for true humanism is always on the side of the revolution.
"We want to put an end to all the former political leaders, to the American imperialism that strangles us, to the tyranny of the military.
We want to start everything and give everyone their chance in life.
We want guajiros, that is, peasants, to stop being slaves and that large sugar plantations be divided between those who work for them. ”
This was not said by Fidel Castro, nor by any other leader of the new Cuba.
These words belong to the young Cuban revolutionary from the novel "To Have and Not to Have", written a quarter of a century ago.
... We broke up with Ernest and Mary Hemingway in the hope of meeting again – this time in Moscow.
Sergo Mikoyan, 1960, No 54

judgments.text: Sergo Mikoyan characterized Hemingway's personality as fair, able to enjoy life, sincere, youthful, and cheerful.

Title: U.S. plans to build world's first nuclear fusion power station in 15 years

Content: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) expanded on the Tokamak device, planning to build a compact fusion experiment device, SPARC, with the key being the creation of a powerful superconductive magnet.
Using the principle of nuclear fission, humans have built hundreds of nuclear power stations.
Now, it is beginning to be used for nuclear fusion.
According to the Guardian and other foreign media reports, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) is launching a nuclear fusion research project to build the world's first nuclear fusion power station in the next 15 years and connect it to the power grid.
The station has a design power of 200 megawatts.
The project was developed by MIT and CFS (Commonwealth Fusion Systems), a private enterprise, to transform nuclear fusion from an expensive scientific experiment to an economic commercial project.
The MIT said the project attracted investment from the Italian energy company ENI.
ENI has invested $50 million in CFS, of which $30 million will be used by MIT to study the project over the next three years.
There are two main ways to develop nuclear energy: the fission of heavy elements and the fusion of light elements.
Nuclear fusion produces a large amount of energy higher than nuclear fission, which has long been regarded by the scientific community as the ultimate source of energy for mankind.
The energy produced by a kilogram of nuclear fusion fuel is equivalent to 11,000 tons of coal, and the fuel deuterium and tritium needed for nuclear fusion are stored in a very large amount in nature and can be extracted in seawater.
However, nuclear fusion is highly uncontrollable.
Human control of fusion reaction is mainly based on a ring adjector, which is driven by a bound electromagnetic wave to create an environment and ultra-high temperature for fusion of deuterium and tritium to achieve controlled fusion.
The device is called Tokamak, and its name derives from its keywords: toroidal, kamera, magnet, and kotushka.
At the end of the 20th century, scientists applied the new superconductivity technology to tokamak devices, resulting in the creation of tokamak devices.
Its imitation principle is the thermal fusion reaction within the Sun, so the industry refers to this device as the "artificial sun".
The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) expanded on the Tokamak device, with plans to build a compact fusion experimental device, SPARC.
The key to SPARC is the creation of a powerful superconductive magnet.
MIT and the CFS team plan to complete their research on superconductive magnets over a three-year period.
According to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), the superconductive material is a steel belt coated with yttrium-ba-copper oxide (YBCO) composite material.
Its advantages are high magnetic field strength and low cost.
Currently, China, the European Union, India, Japan, Korea, Russia and the United States are undertaking a project called the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER) Project, which is equivalent to the construction of a large-scale "man-made solar".
According to the ITER project planning, 2007-2025 is the construction phase, the first ignition is achieved at the end of 2025, and the operational phase is entered in 2035.
The project involved seven parties, including the European Union, China, the United States, Japan and Russia.
China joined the ITER program in 2003 and will undertake 12 of the 137 procurement package manufacturing tasks of ITER devices, close to 10% of total tasks.
At the same time, China is also making its own "artificial sun", the all-superconducting Tokamak nuclear fusion experimental device EAST.
In July of last year, EAST achieved a stable 101.2 second stable long-pulse high-tension beam mode and other ions for the first time in the world, creating a new world record.
Duan Xu, vice president of the Southwest Institute of Physics of the Nuclear Industry, said that after nearly 10 years, China's technological research on nuclear fusion has been carried out from the past to the present.
On March 18, according to the Science and Technology Daily, it was learned from the Hefei Institute of Material Science of the Chinese Academy of Science and Technology that its nuclear energy is safe, so China 's anti-neutron irradiated steel (CLAM steel) as a raw material, using 3D printing technology to achieve the trial production of the key components of the fusion reactor, the first wall sample of the coating, and its structure and performance.
This is the first time in China to achieve 3D printing of fusion reactor key parts.
The research shows that 3D printing technology has good application prospects in the manufacture of advanced nuclear energy system complex components such as fusion reactors.

Title: China Science and Technology 2020 ｜ How far is the Chinese Power of the Artificial Sun?

Content: At the Economic Work Conference of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) at the end of 2020, the government deployed eight key tasks for development in 2021.
This meeting of senior officials of the Communist Party of China (CPC) has not only listed "strengthening the strategic and technological power of the country" as the top priority for next year 's economic development, but also openly stated that China should develop high technology through the promotion of national institutional advantages and "solve a number of problems of' neck-and-neck 'as soon as possible."
Looking back to 2020, China has bright eye performance or national strategic deployment in areas such as lunar exploration, Mars exploration, satellite navigation, human deep dive, quantum research, database technology substitution, international participation in nuclear fusion technology, neutrino experiments and wafer manufacturing.
What are the practical implications of scientific and technological research in these fields? What are China's competitive advantages and realistic challenges?
Where is the next direction of development?
The Sun is the source of human energy, and the ultimate source of human energy is still to be found inside the Sun, simulating the fusion reaction within the Sun on Earth, which is controlled nuclear fusion.
The image is an incredible image of the Sun "exploding" released by the National Space Agency (NASA) in 2018.
(Visual China) The Sun is the nearest star to humans and is actually a supernucleus fusion reactor, with 600 million tons of hydrogen per second converted to helium by fusion reaction, during which about 4.2 million tons of net energy is released into the universe, equivalent to 3.78 × 10 ^ 26 joules.
The Earth received only 1.72 × 10 ^ 17 Joules per second, equivalent to about 19 kg of net energy released, resulting in a habitable Earth ecosystem, which can be seen as a powerful source of fusion energy.
Compared with fossil energy such as coal, oil and natural gas, clean energy such as solar energy, and fission energy similar to nuclear energy, nuclear fusion energy has obvious advantages in energy density and environmental protection.
For example, a 1 million kilowatts power plant requires 2.5 million tons of coal per year, 250 trains per 100 units, 110,000 barrels of oil per year, 11 supertankers per year for fuel use, 28 tons of uranium dioxide per year for fission reactors, 5,000 acres of land and storage space for solar energy, and 400 pounds of deuterium for nuclear fusion reactors. With 600 tons of tritium, 1,300 pounds of lithium-6 can meet the needs, and a minivan can be transported.
At the same time, with coal and fuel as fuel, tens of millions of tons of emissions will be generated each year, which is already intolerable to human air pollution and greenhouse effect.
More importantly, compared to the limited storage of fossil energy such as coal, oil and natural gas, the energy density of clean energy such as solar energy and wind energy is low, nuclear fusion energy has a very high energy density and almost unlimited storage capacity.
Deuterium in a liter of seawater releases energy equivalent to 300 litres of gasoline through a nuclear fusion reaction, with more than 45 trillion tons of deuterium in seawater alone, releasing enough energy for humans to use for hundreds of millions of years.
Because of this, nuclear fusion energy is regarded as the "ultimate energy" of mankind, and the so-called controlled fusion is actually a nuclear fusion reaction simulating the interior of the Sun on Earth, thus being called the "artificial solar".
China ’ s conventional binding nuclear fusion experimental device “Shenguang ” has been developed to“ Shenguang III ”. Its ultimate goal is to achieve laser controlled fusion ignition.
The first is how to trigger nuclear fusion. The hydrogen bomb is a high-temperature high pressure triggered fusion reaction formed by an atomic bomb. It is obviously not applicable to controlled fusion. The first is how to control nuclear fusion after the nuclear fusion is triggered, so that nuclear fusion is provided under human control. Energy, not the power of destruction like a hydrogen bomb.
Furthermore, no material on Earth can withstand the high temperature and pressure required for nuclear fusion.
After several decades of development, there are two major technical branches of the world's controlled nuclear fusion research: the inertial bound fusion (ICF) route and the magnetic bound fusion (MCF) route.
The core is that, while nuclear fusion occurs within the device through inertial or magnetic constraints, the entire device operates at an affordable temperature and even at an ultra-low temperature.
For China, both inertial and magnetic, there are research institutions that are constantly working, walking on both legs.
The so-called inertia constraint is the use of laser shock waves to reach extremely high temperatures and pressures on fuel balls, usually containing deuterium and tritium, resulting in a nuclear fusion reaction "ignited" inside the fuel spheres.
Based on the way in which fusion reactions are directly induced by lasers, the results of inertial restraint research can be used to produce pure poly-mutated nuclear weapons, and therefore are mostly conducted by nuclear weapons research institutes in various countries, such as the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in the United States, and the China Institute of Engineering Physics.
The NIF, built by the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in the United States, is the world's most energy-intensive inertial beam fusion experiment device, and the NIF is 215 metres long and 120 metres wide, equivalent to three football fields, which can focus 2 million joules of energy through 192 laser beams to one point.
At present, NIF has successfully achieved "energy gain", i.e. the energy generated by the fusion reaction for the first time exceeds the energy absorbed by the fuel, and also proves the feasibility of using a strong pulse laser to "ignite" artificial thermal fusion.
The “Shenguang III ” device, built in 2015 by the China Institute of Engineering Physics and the Shanghai Institute of Optical Precision Machinery of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is the world ’ s second largest laser driver, behind NIF in the United States.
In addition, similar high-energy laser devices are being built in Russia and France.
National ignition device in the United States (click to view the high-definition picture): + 6 + 6 + 6 Currently, the ICF technology route is still a long way ahead, compared to the magnetic binding fusion fusion route is much brighter, which is called the field of modern nuclear fusion research.
Magnetic binding fusion is currently concentrated on the Tokamak technical route, and the Tokamak device was first built by Igor of the Kurchatov Institute of the Soviet Union.
Igor Tamm, Andrei Sakharov, Lev Artsimovich and others invented it in the 1950s. In 1968, the third international conference on the physics and controlled nuclear fusion of isons was first published — as many as 1KeV isons were shunted by a few milliseconds. New World of Magnetic Constraint Nuclear Fusion Research.
ITER and China 's three-step strategic Tokamak device center is a circular vacuum chamber, the outside is wrapped around the coil, the inside of Tokamak will generate a huge spiral magnetic field, heating the isons to a very high temperature, to achieve the purpose of nuclear fusion.
After several decades of research, the Tokamak device has developed into a superconductive Tokamak stage, and is not unique to the ICF technical route, since the 1950s, international cooperation and exchanges have continued.
In the 1980s, the United States, the Soviet Union, the European Union, and Japan initiated the construction of the International Thermonuclear Fusion Experimental Reactor (ITER).
In 2006, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan, South Korea and the European Union signed an ITER project to build a superconductive Kamak fusion reactor in Kadarasher, southern France, to explore the scientific and engineering feasibility of using fusion energy for power generation.
It is understood that ITER will become the world 's first station level fusion experimental reactor, which is an essential step towards the eventual commercialization of magneto-bound fusion, and is the largest international cooperation project in which China participates as an equal partner for the first time.
+ 13 + 13 + 13 According to the plan, China, the United States, Russia, India, Japan, and South Korea each undertake about 9% of the total budget of 65%. The EU as the provider provides the remaining 45% of the budget.
For example, India is responsible for the manufacture of low temperature constant, the United States is responsible for the central spiral tube, South Korea and the European Union are responsible for the vacuum container, the annular coil in the magnetic body is made by China, Korea, Russia, Japan, the European Union, the polar coil is made by China, Russia, European Union, etc.
The European Union is responsible for the construction and civil engineering, and the China Nuclear Industry Group has successfully awarded the contract for the installation of the TAC-1 installation of the Carmac host. The installation of the low temperature constant device base was successfully completed on 28 May 2020.
It is expected that ITER will complete the construction phase in 2021, start the reactor in the same year, wait for the ion experiment in 2025, and start full deuterium – tritium fusion experiment in 2035.
In addition to participating in the international cooperation of ITER project, the study of magnetic binding fusion in China has been carried out in parallel. Its main responsible units include the Institute of Physics of China Science and Other Ions in Hefei, Anhui Province, and the Southwest Institute of Physics of China Nuclear Industry Group in Chengdu, Sichuan Province.
The advanced experimental superconductive Kamak experimental device (EAST), built in 2005 by the China Institute of Science and Ion Physics, is the world 's first all-superconductive Kamak nuclear fusion test device. In 2006, the discharge was successfully realized. In 2018, the heating power exceeded 10 megawatts, the storage energy of the isons increased to 300,000 joules, and the center temperature of the isons reached 100 million degrees Celsius for the first time.
On December 4, 2020, China ’ s largest and most parametric advanced Torkamak device, China ’ s second M (HL-2M), was built and released for the first time at the Southwest Institute of Physics, marking China ’ s ownership of the design, construction and operation of large advanced Torkamak devices.
On December 4, 2020, China Circulator No. 2 M was built at the Southwest Institute of Physics of the Nuclear Industry in Chengdu.
In fact, the China Institute of Science and Other Ion Physics and the China Nuclear Industry Group Southwest Institute of Physics, as one of the main units of China 's controlled nuclear fusion research, are also the main players in China' s participation in the ITER project and component subcontractor, through participation in the domestic ITER project. Development of related disciplines and industries.
According to Chinese researchers in the field of nuclear fusion, for a long time, the United States, Japan and the European Union have maintained significant advantages in international controlled nuclear fusion research.
Similar to ITER, the Future China Fusion Engineering Experimental Reactor (CFETR) has been planned to complete controlled fusion research in three steps.
In the first phase, by 2021, CFETR began construction; in the second phase, by 2035, it was planned to build a fusion engineering experimental reactor to begin large-scale scientific experiments; and in the third phase, by 2050, the fusion engineering experimental reactor was successfully constructed to build a fusion commercial demonstration reactor to complete the ultimate energy of mankind.
At present, the international community is widely expected to achieve controlled nuclear fusion by 2050.

Title: Pure Thermo Poison: Why 35 Countries Build the World ’ s Largest Thermonuclear Reactor

Content: Pure Thermo Poison: Why 35 countries are building the world ’ s largest thermonuclear reactor The U.S.-USSR Summit in 1985 gave the world one of the most ambitious technological projects: the experimental thermonuclear reactor ITER ("path").
In Provence, in southern France, thousands of scientists and builders are preparing a complex for scientific experiments that can open the way for humanity to the thermonuclear power plants of the future.
Thermonuclear synthesis has long stirred minds.
In theory, such power plants can be four times more efficient than modern nuclear power plants, much cleaner and safer.
They have no problems with uncontrolled chain reactions and highly radioactive waste, and marine water can be used as fuel.
The EU (46% of expenses), the USA, Russia, India, China, South Korea and Japan (each – 9%) work on a multi-billion dollar project.
If there are no further delays and funding problems, ITER will start working at the end of 2025 – 40 years after the talks between Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev in Geneva.
The present time tells about the history, present and future of a unique project in the field of thermonuclear synthesis.
How does thermonuclear energy work is trying to copy the processes that occur inside the stars: there, at ultra-high temperatures and pressure, the nuclei of hydrogen isotopes merge and emit huge energy.
To achieve this on Earth, special conditions are necessary (for example, the temperature is 10 times higher than in the core of the Sun) - they are created in a thermonuclear reactor.
It is based at least on the most common scheme used by ITER – tokamak, shaped like a bagel vacuum chamber with magnetic coils.
The first tokamaks appeared in the USSR in the 1960s, for ITER will build the largest tokamak in the world with a volume of 830 m3.
In tokamak, deuterium and tritium are launched, and heated to temperatures over 150 million degrees Celsius.
The gas turns into a plasma, and so that the plasma of this temperature does not burn all around, it is held at a distance from the walls by a magnetic field; through the plasma itself, a current is passed.
A powerful magnetic field is provided, in turn, by superconducting magnets, which need to be cooled in a vacuum chamber to almost absolute zero – 268 ° C.
Physically, they will be literally half a meter from the hot plasma to 150,000,000 ° C.
Ensuring trouble-free operation of equipment in such conditions is a complex engineering task.
Modern tokamaki emit less energy than it is spent on heating the system, it is not yet possible to adapt them to generate them.
The best result is the British JET, which returns up to 67% of the energy spent.
Due to the size of the ITER structure (it will be a giant with a height of a nine-storey house, and about the same diameter), the creators expect that the reactor will be able to allocate energy ten times more than it is spent on plasma heating (to give 500 MW from 50 MW).
This point is fundamental for the construction of thermonuclear power plants in the future.
But ITER will not produce electricity: all the allocated energy will only be spent on heating the walls of the tokamak.
Although if the experiments with ITER are successful, the next stage (from 2030) will be the prototype of a thermonuclear reactor for power plants, DEMO – they should appear in the 2040-50s.
India, Russia, South Korea and Japan expressed their desire to build such reactors.
The most important goal of ITER is to show the possibility of generating energy by a thermonuclear reactor.
This will require the controlled production of "burning plasma" (with it the synthesis reaction will be self-sustaining) and the self-reproduction of tritium, a rather rare isotope used as fuel.
In addition, ITER should demonstrate how modern technologies are ready for the construction of commercial thermonuclear power plants, as well as assess their reliability and safety.
Safety is one of the key advantages of thermonuclear reactors over conventional nuclear ones.
There is no chain reaction with consequences: in case of plasma problems, it will instantly cool down and fade, ITER notes.
What is better with the radioactivity of the fuel: tritium, a weak source of beta radiation, will be generated directly in the reactor.
The design of the reactor involves several barriers to radioactive substances arising during operation.
The half-life of radioactive waste for most isotopes in a thermonuclear reactor is about 10 years, whereas for individual components of spent nuclear fuel these values can be thousands or even millions of years.
From zero to 63% In November 1985, at a meeting in Geneva, the leaders of the United States and the USSR agreed on a joint study of thermonuclear energy for peaceful purposes – this was the beginning of the project.
A year later, he was Euroate, the USSR, the United States and Japan.
Work on the ITER design began in 1988 and continued until the final version was approved in 2001.
In 2003, China and South Korea joined the ITER consortium, and India joined the ITER consortium in 2005.
At the same time, a place for construction was chosen: the vicinity of Saint-Paul-les-Durants in Provence, France, near the research center for nuclear power Kadarash.
The Inter-State Agreement on the Establishment of ITER was signed by the Ministers of the participating countries on November 21, 2006, and in October 2007, ITER Organization, a legal entity responsible for the construction, operation and subsequent dismantling of the reactor, began its work.
The site began to cook in 2007, build - in 2010.
In parallel, the participating countries began to work on the elements of the ITER complex: India is building a cryostat for the project, the US is developing a central magnetic coil (its strength is enough to lift the aircraft carrier), the EU and Korea are preparing a vacuum chamber, China and Russia supply superconductors (a total of 100,000 km of such conductors), part of the coils and various electrical components, Japan is preparing toroidal field coils.
As of the end of June 2019, the project was ready "by more than 63%", noted in ITER Organization.
More than 70% of the buildings have been completed, the installation of the first components of the reactor itself has begun.
The full phase of installation should begin next year, as the construction and delivery of all the necessary components: for example, China on September 23 built the first 400-ton magnetic coil, it will be delivered to the site of ITER construction by December.
In terms of complexity and manufacturability, ITER surpasses many large-scale scientific buildings of the century, including the Big Hadron Collider.
"A collider is just a vacuum plant that accelerates a bunch of protons, it's a simpler level task.
ITER is a physics of plasma, and plasma is so many degrees of freedom, so much instability, all of them need to be dealt with, - said Radio Svoboda, head of the Russian agency of the ITER project Anatoly Krasilnikov. - In terms of a large number of parameters that need to be taken into account at the same time, ITER, of course, is a much more complex problem than a collider.
Well, ITER is more expensive. "
Such a complex international project based on advanced technologies is really expensive.
If at the start the project budget was estimated at €5 billion, then by 2017 it had already reached the level of €20 billion: the total figure is difficult to estimate, as governments themselves determine the level of expenditure on certain components produced by them.
Participants of the project transfer not money, but transfer the built components.
In the Russian budget for ITER in 2020-22, 11.8 billion rubles (about $180 million) were invested.
Not only ITER, the Bublic-Tokomak is not the only option for thermonuclear synthesis considered by science.
Alternative ways are studied not only in large government institutions, but also in small startups.
They are now in the world, according to Bloomberg estimates, more than two dozen.
However, major breakthroughs and controlled commercial energy production have not yet been reported.
The nearest analogue of the current cell is a ratchet, also a toroidal, "bagle-like" system, with all its similarity does not require maintaining the current in the plasma.
Such an installation has its pros and cons, the largest and most successful at the moment - German Wendelstein 7-X.
On it, German researchers set a number of records, although in terms of characteristics and scale, it is far from ITER.
The Commonwealth Fusion Systems startup, based on MIT, promises to build a much smaller, cheaper, while slightly less efficient than ITER, SPARC.
How do they manage to do that?
Scientists hope to apply the latest high-temperature superconductors and are going to show solutions in the next two years.
Another non-standard option is thermonuclear synthesis with inertial holding.
It uses lasers on all sides "crimping" and heating the miniature fuel capsule deuterium pulses, imitating the processes occurring during the explosion of a hydrogen bomb.
The largest scientific organization in the world that applies this approach is the National Ignition Facility in the United States, where 193 beams of powerful lasers are used for this purpose.
Canadian General Fusion and American Tri Alpha Energy use their own, even more exotic methods of thermonuclear fusion, but alas, no one has yet introduced commercially ready solutions.
Why and when?
Critics believe that thermonuclear synthesis is too expensive and commercially inefficient, and they are encouraged to invest, for example, in renewable energy.
ITER does not deny its importance, but emphasizes that the creation of new clean energy sources with a constant generation level (independent of, say, the number of sunny days or wind power) remains an important task.
Thermonuclear energy will not replace renewable energy, but will serve together with it as an even better alternative to traditional "dirty" sources of energy, says ITER.
The only question is when it happens.
The first launch is planned for December 2025 ("the best technically achievable date") using hydrogen, then helium, deuterium will be added and finally full-fledged work on deuterium tritium is planned in 2035: only then can a tenfold recoil in power be achieved.
The project completion dates have already shifted, and given its complexity, it is unlikely that there will be no further delays.
In addition, despite all attempts, thermonuclear synthesis may be too expensive for industrial applications at the current stage of technology development.
Skeptics say that "thermo poison is the source of energy of the future, and will always remain so."
In a few years, humanity will be able to cool the fervor of skeptics or back up their positions.
Given the complexity of the topic, it is unlikely that someone is ready to guarantee deadlines in such projects.
